item.title: The fans at the FA Cup game no-one could see
item.description: Ian Kirke struggled to watch his side's FA Cup first round match against Altrincham due to thick fog [Ian Kirke] For many football fans, an FA Cup win is the stuff of dreams. But for 690 Notts County supporters, thick fog meant they could barely see it happen. Ian Kirke was among the Magpies fans whose view of Saturday's FA Cup first-round tie against Altrincham was obscured by fog, leaving many unable to see the League One side's penalty shootout victory. The thick layer of fog provided chaos not just for the players and fans, but also commentators and camera operators at the J Davidson Stadium. Kirke said fans had to rely on the cheers - or silence - from the home support during the shootout. "It's the most bonkers festival of football I've ever seen in my life," he added. Heavy fog meant Notts County fans were unable to watch the penalty shootout that took place at the other end of the pitch [Getty Images] Lifelong fan Kirke, who lives in Berkshire, said the weather at kick-off was "like any normal match". Before fog descended over Greater Manchester, Jacob Bedeau had given Notts County the lead just before the half-hour mark. The hosts, who play in the National League, hit back as Lucas Weaver and Lewis Banks scored to give Altrincham a 2-1 lead. With the conditions worsening, referee David Rock opted to continue with the tie, which saw the camera often unable to pick up the ball. The referee's decision to continue the game paid off for Notts County, who levelled the tie at 2-2, when Callum Roberts scored from the edge of the box. "I can just about see the bright white numbers on their shirts, but I am struggling to see what is happening on the far side of the pitch," said BBC Radio Nottingham commentator Adam Hassell. Former Notts County striker Mark Stallard was also commentating on BBC Radio Nottingham, and said: "We're looking around, and here in the press box no-one knows where the ball is! It's like a spot the ball competition. "We genuinely cannot see the linesman or the players on the far side. It's slightly farcical having to commentate for radio listeners." Lynda Lally said the fog got worse during the second half [Dan Westwell] Fellow Magpies fan Lynda Lally, from Beeston in Nottinghamshire, said the weather got "worse and worse" after half-time. "For the other 45 minutes, we could only see what was happening once players emerged from the fog," she said. The weather became "a cross between an eerie Christmas nativity gone horribly wrong - and the 1980s film called The Fog," Kirke said. Kirke added the fog that led to an FA Cup third-round replay between Notts County and Wimbledon being abandoned in 2001 "wasn't as bad" as it was at Altrincham. "I don't know what on earth had to happen for the referee to call it off," he said. With the game going to penalties, Lally had hoped the shootout would take place in front of the Notts County fans so she could finally see the ball. item.title: Sharks Win! Stenberg Scores & Wins It in 3-2 Shootout
item.description: The San Jose Sharks welcome the New York Islanders into SAP Center. Ivar Stenberg and Tyler Toffoli scored, and the Sharks won 3-2 in the shootout! I apologize for the short article here, will update in a couple hours. I had to take my dog Mushu to the ER right before the game (she’s okay!), will watch the game and add more shortly. Period 1 Hutton goal: Gotta re-watch, strange-looking on replay. Stenberg goal: Dellandrea keeps it in, Stenberg heads to the net, Toffoli fires it, deflection and in. Period 2 Eklund goal: Dellandrea looked a step slow on Eklund. It was in recovery, Dellandrea hedged harder toward Schaefer, probably the game plan, and Eklund found the soft spot. Toffoli goal: I hope Pelech is okay lol…haven’t seen that before, off Pelech’s face and in. I can add the lol because Pelech back in there and shot wasn’t too hard. Period 3 Marchment penalty: I might understand giving Marchment an extra, he looked like he was getting some shots in when Eklund was covered up and the refs were shielding him, but how does Eklund not even get one boarding minor on that? 10 in: Redemption for the PK? Goodrow nice job to skate it out, good pop, then Ostapchuk draws the trip, and Palat gets the hooking. The rare double make-up call lol. 8 left: San Jose Sharks with some chances 4-on-3. Hope Celebrini isn’t kicking himself after the game. He had one in the slot. I can tell that he’s taking all this losing very hard. Smith hit a post too. Good PP. Celebrini-Smith-Wennberg-Stenberg when they needed a goal there. 5 left: Misa comes up with the Pohlkamp stretch, and Islander draped over him, still gets a shot. 1 left: Nurse versus Homstrom low, Wennberg swooped in to outnumber, kill the play, Kesselring comes out with it. Value of Wennberg there. No rest for Wennberg and Smith! Regulation ATOI: Wennberg 21:41, Celebrini 21:16, Smith 21:09. Wennberg led San Jose Sharks forwards. First Sharks’ point in six games, well-earned. OT Wennberg-Celebrini-Dickinson to start. When Misa on the ice in OT, Celebrini gives him the puck and hides way in the NZ. Fun cat-and-mouse game there with Isles’ defense. 2 left: Wennberg just ripped it from Palmieri along the wall. He looks healthy. Related Headlines Preview/Lines #20: Wennberg Back, How Have They Missed Him Most? item.title: Cooper Flagg Addresses Growing Impact And Improved Offense After Another Historic Outing
item.description: Nov 9, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; Dallas Mavericks forward Cooper Flagg (32) celebrates making a three point shot during the second half against the Indiana Pacers at the American Airlines Center. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images As the face of the Dallas Mavericks franchise, there have been several eyes on Cooper Flagg entering his sophomore season. Despite the inherent pressure of carrying a franchise at just 19 years old, it is safe to say that the Mavericks’ superstar has delivered. On the second night of a back-to-back, Cooper Flagg dropped a historic performance of 43 points, 10 rebounds, six assists, and three steals to lead the Mavericks to a clutch 125-122 victory over the Indiana Pacers . Aside from marking his fifth 40-point game, this stat line also sees him emerge as the first teenager to notch a 40/10/5/3 game in NBA history . Purely from an individual perspective, this is spectacular. However, the fact that it results in wins for the Mavericks is equally promising. On that note, during his postgame media availability , Cooper Flagg addressed his growing impact and how he has improved as a scorer in clutch situations. “It just speaks to the type of basketball I’ve always played and how I was raised being a true competitor,” Flagg shared about his impact. “Whenever I get out there on the court, it just goes back to being a competitor and trying to make as many winning plays as I can. I’m trying to make the easy, right basketball play out there. It just speaks to that. My teammates put me in good positions. My coaches trust me to go out there and make plays.” In the fourth quarter, Cooper Flagg scored the first basket to bring the Mavs level at 93-93. After this point, the 19-year-old went on a tear, notching a total of 16 points, which included the clutch basket to extend Dallas’ lead to four points with less than 30 seconds on the clock. Flagg’s poise and composure in these clutch situations speak volumes about his development in the brief span of one season. To that end, the forward attributes this to the work he put into improving his offensive repertoire over the summer, stating : “Just being able to get to my spots at a higher level and being more comfortable with that. That’s allowed me to take a little bit of a load off my body, stopping short, and raising up over people. It’s taxing to get downhill and all the way to the rim and try to finish over 7-footers all night, every night. Just adding that in there it allows me to pace myself a bit and steal some easy ones.” “But again, just trusting the work that I put in all summer long and being comfortable with those shots,” he added. “I think it goes back to my teammates too, just trusting me with make or miss and getting to those spots. When I’m in that mindset that no matter what, as long as I’m getting the shot, that I’m comfortable with, it’s going to be a good outcome for our team.” It goes without saying that Cooper Flagg’s growth has been a rewarding sight for Ma

item.title: Bills blast listless Vikings for week 9 MNF win
item.description: Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images Bills blast listless Vikings for week 9 MNF win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Buffalo Bills forced frustration out of the Minnesota Vikings fanbase . Fans went from loud “Skol” chants to boos, as Buffalo pummeled the Vikings 23-6 on Monday Night Football. Coach Joe Brady and quarterback Josh Allen collaborated to shred a Brian Flores-led defense. Allen even overcame a stunning hustle interception from Byron Murphy in the end zone . The star QB retaliated by hitting Keleki Latu on a 25-yard touchdown pass that eventually blew the game open. Allen finished with 234 passing yards and one touchdown. Running back James Cook III piled 107 yards and scored late too. The Bills take care of business for the win over the Vikings on Monday Night Football 🔥 Josh Allen : 21/31 234 passing yards 1 passing TD James Cook III: 107 yards 1 TD pic.twitter.com/vVXVYlSuEq — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 10, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Cook pierced the dagger in and sent the loud Vikings fans into the exits with his red zone scoring run. James Cook RUNS it in for the Bills TD 😤 The hold a 20-6 lead in the fourth! pic.twitter.com/Nhm1ThLYm0 — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 10, 2026 So Allen was supposed to face one of the league’s most talented and brilliant defensive coaches. Plus a man he previously faced a lot in the former Miami Dolphins head coach Flores. Yet Allen saw cracks in the Vikings’ coverage, including locating the one-on-ones and winning that battle. Josh Allen finds Ty Johnson for a HUGE 36-yard catch 😤 pic.twitter.com/W8UKzrQrWS — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 10, 2026 Buffalo’s defense came through in lights out fashion too, with Dorian Williams dropping into coverage and grabbing this errant throw from backup quarterback Carson Wentz. Dorian Williams COMES UP with the interception 😤 Bills ball! pic.twitter.com/6mEQ1M1u8D — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 10, 2026 Wentz took over QB1 duties with starting passer Kyler Murray injured and sitting out. Now the Bills have handed the Vikings their second straight loss, but this one coming in what was supposed to be a possible Super Bowl preview. Especially with both teams walking into Minneapolis with identical 6-1 records. Yet it’s the Bills who look very much like the stronger contender in dismantling the NFC’s best team. Related: Bills’ Greg Rousseau reveals how Buffalo’s defense put Carson Wentz ‘in hell’ on MNF Related: Bills secure best start in over 3 decades after Vikings MNF beatdown

item.title: Victor Wembanyama reveals he wants to take the next step as a dominant center
item.description: Victor Wembanyama reveals he wants to take the next step as a dominant center originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After a slow start to the 2026-27 NBA season, some people were hesitant to keep calling Victor Wembanyama the MVP favorite. Of course, he has returned to top form, as he is playing like the best player in the league at the moment. The San Antonio Spurs now have a 9-2 record after beating the Phoenix Suns on Monday. Wembanyama had yet another landmark performance, as he posted a stat line of 40 points, 11 rebounds, and nine blocks. Victor Wembanyama believes he's not the complete player just yet Despite having one of the best runs a center has had in the NBA this season, Wembanyama believes that he is not the finished article just yet. Of course, he is correct with that assessment, but it goes to show his elite mentality because he is already having some generational performances. The last four games, in particular, have been remarkable. He has only played 27.5 minutes per game during this stretch, but he is averaging 37.7 points and five blocks per game. It is an impressive look into his dominance and how he can decide games early on with his impact. MORE: Victor Wembanyama reveals the lesson he learned from Gregg Popovich Wembanyama has clearly cemented himself as one of the leading candidates for the MVP award alongside the Los Angeles Lakers ' Luka Doncic. The Slovenian might have the leg up in scoring and playmaking, but Wembanyama is matching him well with scoring and defending. Despite those strengths, it looks like Wembanyama still wants to keep improving. If he is already this good as an unfinished product, that spells trouble for the rest of the NBA. "There are a lot of things I still want to do, but I need to get better first. As the years go on and my conditioning gets better, it allows me to keep developing on both sides of the floor," Wembanyama said about what he needs to keep improving on moving forward . In the long run, Wembanyama will be an even more dangerous player. He has all the tools to become one of the league's best-ever players, and he wants to keep adding to his skill set. item.title: Coachella Valley's Chris Mañon scores career-high 32 points in win over San Diego
item.description: Coachella Valley Lakers guard Chris Mañon (30) goes up for a shot during an NBA G League basketball game against the Salt Lake City Stars, Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, at Acrisure Arena in Palm Desert, Calif. PALM DESERT, Calif. — Behind Chris Mañon’s career-high 32 points and 13 rebounds, the Coachella Valley Lakers started the season 2-0 after a 124-110 win over the San Diego Clippers on Monday night. Mañon set the tone early with 16 points in the first quarter. Mañon also added a steal and two blocks. His previous career high came almost a year to the day on Nov. 10, 2025, when he had 31 points against the Valley Suns. “I did know, I thought it was 33 but it was 31 last year. I could’ve had 40 tonight, but maybe tomorrow,” Mañon said postgame. “It's my bread and butter,” turning defense into offense, Mañon said. “Being that point of attack defender is something I take a lot of pride in on the defensive side.” The difference between this year and last year for Mañon has been his offensive output. “Just playing with more confidence, playing with joy, not being afraid to make mistakes,” Mañon said. For Mañon, he’s staying patient while on a two-way contract with the Lakers. He spoke about remaining patient throughout the process. Wikipedia “Just controlling what I can control. I'll say this, first half I was a little more patient, second half not so much. Ultimately, I think I can do a better job with my mentality.” When asked about Mañon’s career high in points scored, head coach Zack Cerda said it all started with his defense. “It really started with his defense, being a good point of attack defender. He’s just a tone setter for us on the defensive end. Offensively he’s able to attack closeouts. He makes good decisions, two-on-one reads in the paint, getting to the free-throw line. He’s a great downhill player, applying great pressure on the defense.” For Mañon, the focus has been on improving his shot. “He can shoot it,” Cerda said. “He’s been putting in a lot of time on his shot working with coach Liam Flynn.” Four of the five Lakers starters scored in double figures: Cole Swider added 21 points, Jahmir Young had 21 points, and Arthur Kaluma had 16 points on 6-of-12 shooting from the field. Coachella Valley dominated on the glass, outrebounding San Diego 49-30. 17 of the 49 rebounds were offensive. Cerda credited the team's practice drill called “Set the Tone” for their effective rebounding. “It looks like a football practice out there when we’re working on rebounding,” Cerda said. Mañon led the team with 13 rebounds. San Diego fell to 1-1 on the new season. The Clippers made three more field goals than Coachella Valley following a fourth-quarter scoring run that cut a 28-point lead down to 15. The Lakers tightened defense to close out the win. A quick turnaround for both teams as the second half of the back-to-back takes place Tuesday at 7 p.m. PST at Acrisure Arena.

item.title: ‘Like Rudy Gobert’ – NFL fans ruthlessly call out major Minnesota Vikings flaw after MNF loss
item.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings offence was exposed against the Buffalo Bills on Monday night, and fans online are letting them hear it. The Minnesota Vikings suffered their second straight loss after a 23-6 defeat to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night. Quarterback Carson Wentz had an extremely poor game, completing just 8 of 25 passes for 81 yards and throwing two interceptions. Buffalo’s defence made life miserable for Minnesota, they managed to limit Justin Jefferson to just three catches for 58 yards. James Cook rushed for 107 yards and a touchdown as the Bills pulled away in the second half, handing the Vikings just their second defeat of the year. NFL fans were not amused by watching the Minnesota Vikings offence struggle, but did make fun of them for it Minnesota began their campaign with a 6-0 run, but the problems with the offence have been a consistent theme. Their defence has limited teams significantly, allowing them to put up a run despite averaging less than 20 points per game as a team through their first eight games. Teams can get away with obvious flaws sometimes when the wins keep coming. After their second consecutive loss, though, it seems that fans have lost their patience with the Vikings. “The Minnesota Vikings are like if Rudy Gobert was an NFL team,” one fan hilariously said. “This is the most accurate comparison of all time lol,” another agreed. “The Vikings QB situation is so bad that Joe Buck & Troy Aikman are repairing their relationship by laughing at our QBs,” a third fan posted. “Vikings should be calling Bengals about Joe Flacco at this point,” a fourth fan claimed. “Lowest QBR in years the night before the trade deadline. That’s not a game, that’s a cry for help, fam,” a fifth fan said. “The Vikings deserve all this and more, some people were getting delusional after that 6-0 start,” a sixth fan commented. Gobert is known for being one of the most dominant defensive players in NBA history, but his offence leaves a lot to be desired. The Vikings being compared to the big man is both hilarious, and sadly true at the moment. The franchise really needs to address their quarterback situation, and quickly. item.title: Warriors Suffer Another Setback As Brandon Williams Could Miss Extended Time After Hamstring Injury
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, CA - NOVEMBER 7: Brandon Williams #12 of the Golden State Warriors handles the ball during the game against the Orlando Magic on November 7, 2026 at Chase Center in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Jed Jacobsohn/NBAE via Getty Images) The Golden State Warriors faced the New Orleans Pelicans tonight and destroyed them 138-87 at the Chase Center in San Francisco. But early in the first quarter, they faced another injury setback when Brandon Williams left for the locker room with less than four minutes left, after scoring four points on 2-for-3 shooting (66.7% FG). The 26-year-old guard did not return for the rest of the night, joining players like Jimmy Butler , Will Richard, and Moses Moody on the Warriors’ extended injury list. The team later announced it has scheduled an MRI for tomorrow, November 10, to better understand the extent of the issue before suggesting any timeline for his return. “As per Warriors’ PR, Brandon Williams will undergo an MRI on his left hamstring. If Williams misses extended time, that’s another blow to the Warriors’ backcourt depth with Will Richard also out,” wrote ClutchPoints’ Warriors reporter, Kenzo Fukuda, on X. Williams has been coming off the bench and consistently been impactful for the Warriors. He has averaged 10.4 points, 2.3 assists, and 2.1 rebounds while shooting 41.3% from the field and 30.4% from beyond the arc. This will be another setback for a roster already plagued by injuries. “It’s a big concern; he’s a huge part of our team. And he’s given us a lift. It’s a hamstring thing; we’ll get an MRI, and we’ll see how that is,” head coach Steve Kerr said during the postgame press conference. L.J. Cryer played extended minutes in Williams’ absence as Golden State extended their winning streak to eight games and improved to 8-3 for the season. Veterans like Draymond Green and Stephen Curry played only 21 minutes each tonight, a silver lining in a low-effort night for the Warriors. They have plenty of reasons to feel confident after extending their winning streak to eight games, but Brandon Williams’ injury is an unfortunate development that could complicate their rotation. The Warriors have benefited from having reliable contributors come off the bench, with Williams providing valuable scoring and playmaking whenever called upon. His ability to handle the ball and create opportunities for himself has been particularly important with several other guards already sidelined. If his hamstring injury forces him to miss an extended period, the Warriors will have to rely more heavily on their remaining backcourt options, potentially adding responsibilities to L.J. Cryer and the other available guards. With an MRI scheduled for Tuesday, the team will have a clearer picture of his recovery timeline soon. For now, the team will hope its impressive momentum continues without another significant blow to its depth. They now face the Rockets on Wednesday night, November 11. It will be a big challenge f

item.title: Bills at Vikings Week 9 instant analysis: Buffalo batters Minnesota
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates as he walks off the field after defeating the Minnesota Vikings in the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills walked out of U.S. Bank Stadium with a 23-6 win on Monday Night Football . Here’s everything I wrote down along the way. 1st Half Joe Brady chose to start with the ball on offense again. You have to be very secure you’ll make them pay with it. A 3-and-out going backwards shows they weren’t good enough for this choice. James Cook has to catch those checkdowns. 2nd game in a row he starts with a drop. Pre-snap penalties by the OL with 2 backups in a loud venue are expected, unfortunately. The Bills WRs have to be able to beat their matchups quickly, or Brian Flores will send everybody after Josh Allen all night. Josh must have an easy button against it, and DJ Moore is my hope here. Great 1st defensive drive by the Bills. Quick 3-and-out. The Vikings’ offense isn’t anything special, but with the way Buffalo’s D played before the bye, we couldn’t be sure about them being able to do that to start the game. 2nd offensive drive, and the run game has struggled so far, but they must be patient with it. Josh has 2 quick completions on 3rd downs against the blitz, to Moore and Khalil Shakir. Easy buttons start to appear as the Bills use motion pre-snap to confuse the Vikings D. A Josh Allen intentional grounding penalty put the O in a bad spot in a promising drive until that point. Man coverage on a PA bootleg play, and Josh couldn’t get the ball to the line of scrimmage as he was tackled by Andrew Van Ginkel. 3rd and long, and Josh airs it out as he gets hit. Moore was open deep, but the ball seemed to go too inside, giving time to the opposite-side CB to make the play on the ball. It was kind of an arm punt, but the return was great. Tylan Grable made a great play to stop it at midfield. Defense’s back on the field and making plays. I think it was a backward pass, and the Bills will have the ball. Brady with a good challenge here. After the replay, Bills ball. Also after the replay, the INT was an awesome play by Byron Murphy. No way Josh could have expected it from him. First Bills points on a Tyler Bass FG. Every point should be valuable today, game of patience. 3-0 Bills. Whoa, Tommy Doman forcing a fumble , and it flies right to the arms of another Vikings player. The Bills almost create another TO. Bills D continues to succeed as Justin Jefferson gets hurt. Everything’s under control on that side of the ball so far. Offense has to take care of the ball and play safe, be patient. The O strategy hasn’t worked. They have to insist on the run game, but they can’t have Josh under center on obvious passing downs. The OL is struggling to deal with those pressure packages. item.title: Warriors Player Ratings: Curry Drops An Efficient 25 To Blow Out Pelicans In Lopsided Matchup
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images The Golden State Warriors delivered an absolute demolition of the New Orleans Pelicans , cruising to a 138-87 victory behind an explosive offensive performance. Stephen Curry finished with 25 points on efficient shooting (6-10), but he wasn’t even the Warriors’ leading scorer in a game where the entire rotation was scorching hot. Yaxel Lendeborg and Brandin Podziemski each scored 25 points, combining for 19-29 shooting from the field. Lendeborg was particularly impressive, knocking down all four of his three-point attempts while contributing seven rebounds and four assists. Podziemski matched the scoring total with five triples of his own. Golden State shot an incredible 54.9% from the field and 47.7% from three-point range, compared to New Orleans’ miserable 36.3% and 28.6%, respectively. The Warriors also dominated the glass 50-31, dished out 37 assists, and finished with a staggering 51-point largest lead. Here are the Warriors’ player ratings from the blowout victory. Stephen Curry: A+ Game Stats: 25 PTS, 5 REB, 2 AST, 1 TOV, 6-10 FG, 4-7 3-PT FG, 9-9 FT, 21 MIN Curry was incredibly efficient, scoring 25 points in just 21 minutes while shooting 60.0% from the field and making four three-pointers. He also converted all nine free throws, barely wasting a scoring opportunity. The Warriors didn’t need Curry to play extended minutes, and the superstar made the most of his time on the floor. An efficient scoring performance with minimal turnovers is exactly what Golden State wants from its leader. Yaxel Lendeborg: A+ Game Stats: 23 PTS, 7 REB, 4 AST, 1 STL, 2 TOV, 8-10 FG, 4-4 3-PT FG, 3-4 FT, 27 MIN Lendeborg was spectacular. He finished with 23 points on just 10 shot attempts, including a perfect 4-4 performance from beyond the arc. His efficiency was remarkable, and he contributed seven rebounds and four assists along the way. Golden State received a tremendous two-way performance from Lendeborg, who finished with a team-high +34. This was precisely the kind of performance that makes a blowout even more convincing. Brandin Podziemski: A+ Game Stats: 25 PTS, 2 REB, 4 AST, 1 STL, 1 BLK, 10-19 FG, 5-11 3-PT FG, 26 MIN Podziemski matched Curry’s scoring total while taking on a larger offensive workload. His five three-pointers helped Golden State completely overwhelm New Orleans from the perimeter. Although he wasn’t quite as efficient as Lendeborg, Podziemski’s 25 points and four assists were instrumental in the offensive explosion. Zero turnovers made his performance even better. Al Horford: A- Game Stats: 5 PTS, 2 REB, 6 AST, 2 STL, 3 BLK, 2-5 FG, 1-3 3-PT FG, 15 MIN Horford was outstanding defensively and as a facilitator. Six assists, two steals, and three blocks in only 15 minutes represent an impressive all-around contribution. He also knocked down a three-pointer, helping maintain Golden State’s offensive spacing. Horford’s versatility was on full display in this dominant performance. Charles Basse

item.title: Oluwo seeks Yoruba language as medium for teaching science
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Oluwo of Iwo, Oba Abdulrosheed Akanbi, has called for the development and promotion of Yoruba language as a medium of instruction for academic subjects, including Physics and other specialised courses. The monarch made the call on Monday during the 2026 Odun Olodumare celebration and his 11th coronation anniversary at his palace in Iwo, Osun State. Oba Akanbi said Yoruba had the capacity to serve as a language of instruction across different academic disciplines if deliberate efforts were made to develop and expand its use. “Normally, I prefer to speak my Yoruba language. I want to upgrade the Yoruba language so that we can use it to teach Physics and all kinds of subjects and courses in the educational system,” he said. The traditional ruler also advocated the preservation and modernisation of Yoruba culture, particularly the reform of traditions he said promoted violence. While praising the richness of Yoruba heritage, he stressed the need to preserve its positive aspects while addressing practices that could encourage violence. “When it comes to culture, I want a culture that is free of violence. I accept all Yoruba cultures and traditions, but those that need modifications, particularly traditions that promote violence, must be addressed. “It is not that I totally reject them, but I understand that change takes time,” he said. The monarch also announced a N5 million empowerment scheme for at least 100 residents of Iwo, with each beneficiary expected to receive N50,000. He said the beneficiaries would be drawn from different segments of the community, including members of the royal institution, princes, chiefs, the Muslim community, traditional initiates and ordinary residents. According to him, beneficiaries will be selected randomly rather than through a predetermined process. The 2026 Odun Olodumare celebration also attracted members of different religious groups to the palace, where they offered prayers and praises to God for the monarch, his subjects, Iwo town and the country. The post Oluwo seeks Yoruba language as medium for teaching science appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ian Garry Takes Pride in Short-Notice Fight History Ahead of Yaroslav Amosov Showdown
item.description: UFC Saudi Arabia was officially announced just days ago, with a stacked Fight Night card scheduled for December 5 at the ANB Arena in Riyadh. The main event will see Israel Adesanya take on Shara Magomedov, but another matchup has already caught the attention of MMA fans. Ian Garry’s five-round co-main event clash against Yaroslav Amosov is being dubbed the “people’s main event.” Amosov enters the contest with a prodigal 30-1 professional record, although this will be only his third appearance inside the Octagon. Garry, meanwhile, is coming off a defeat to Islam Makhachev in the main event of UFC 330 , where he challenged for the welterweight championship. Despite losing, the Irishman gave the Dagestani one of his toughest tests since his first meeting with Alexander Volkanovski at UFC 284. View this post on Instagram A post shared by HOME OF FIGHT (@homeoffight) ALSO READ: Dana White Turns Down Donald Trump’s Press Secretary Offer in Hilarious Exchange at White House Now, ‘The Future’ faces another dangerous opponent in Amosov, a former Bellator champion who was widely regarded as the best welterweight outside the UFC for several years. However, taking on elite competition on short notice is nothing new for Garry, who has consistently accepted difficult challenges throughout his career. The Irishman recently reminded fans of that record with a six-word message on social media. Fighters Only Magazine initially shared a graphic highlighting Garry’s short-notice assignments against Shavkat Rakhmonov , Carlos Prates, and now Amosov, with the Irishman accepting the respective fights on 21, 25, and 27 days’ notice. While the achievement is impressive given the caliber of opposition, Garry took to the comments to point out that the publication had overlooked another short-notice assignment: his fight against former champion Belal Muhammad, which he accepted on 28 days’ notice. He also reminded the outlet about his bout against Michael “Venom” Page. Garry wrote, “Belal Muhammad 28 days notice. MVP too.” The publication subsequently acknowledged the omission in another post, writing, “Ian Machado Garry points out that we missed a couple. Sorry Ian…won’t happen again.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Fighters Only (@fightersonlymag) Garry’s short-notice resume dates back to UFC 303 on June 29, 2024, when he defeated Michael “Venom” Page via unanimous decision. He then stepped up to face Shavkat Rakhmonov at UFC 310 on December 7, 2024, replacing the original main-event plans in a five-round title eliminator. Although he lost via unanimous decision, the performance further established his credentials as an elite welterweight contender. Garry bounced back against Carlos Prates at UFC Kansas City on April 26, 2025, accepting the main-event opportunity on roughly a month’s notice before securing another unanimous decision victory. He then defeated former welterweight champion Belal Muhammad via unanimous decision at UFC Qatar on November 22, 2025

item.title: Mets post a meme reaction after Carson Benge missed out on NL ROY honor
item.description: David Frerker-Imagn Images Mets post a meme reaction after Carson Benge missed out on NL ROY honor appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . New York Mets outfielder Carson Benge came up short as Sal Stewart won NL Rookie of the Year. Benge finished with seven first-place votes and 107 points, a distant second to Stewart’s 170. The Cardinals’ JJ Wetherholt went third with 99 points. In response to Benge’s tough loss, the Mets’ official X account posted the “sitting wolf meme” with a Mets cap placed on its head. pic.twitter.com/jqtPnmiKVy Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — New York Mets (@Mets) November 10, 2026 The meme is often used to depict solitude and loneliness, which some Mets fans may be feeling after Benge missed out on the award. The Mets rookie was one of the few bright spots in another disappointing season that finished 74-88. Benge hit .282 with 20 home runs (third on the team behind Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor) and 65 RBIs. He also broke Pete Alonso’s Mets rookie record for most hits , finishing the season with a team-leading 168. Of the three Rookie of the Year finalists, Stewart, Benge, and Wetherholt, Benge was perhaps the most well-rounded option. Aside from being solid with the bat, he was also a plus on baserunning and defense, which were big knocks on Stewart. Moreover, Benge finished a close second to Wetherholt in FanGraphs WAR (4.3 to 4.6) among rookies, while Stewart was well behind at 2.0. There are several unknowns facing the Mets this offseason, one of them being Francisco Lindor’s future. But one thing that is clear is that Carson Benge is one of the team’s centerpieces moving forward. With him and Juan Soto in the outfield, the Mets should have a solid foundation to build upon for the next few years. item.title: Nixa soccer gets revenge over bogey team Glendale in district championship
item.description: SPRINGFIELD — Revenge is a dish best served cold. On a chilly evening, Nixa soccer bested Glendale 1-0 behind a late goal to lift the Class 4 district championship on Monday, Nov. 9. This was Nixa’s first victory over Glendale since 2023, after losing five straight games. It’s a moment that many of the seniors have been dreaming of, especially goalkeeper Jackson Smith. “It feels great, senior year, we haven’t beat them since freshman year,” Smith said. “For us to come out and win a district championship, it feels good for our city, our team. I’m thrilled.” Smith had a stellar game, but when a hero was needed, Gavin Shaw rose to the occasion. Cross country: Gloria Deo's Caroline Fields wins Class 1 state title with sister by her side With three minutes remaining, Shaw received the ball on the left wing. The senior danced on the ball a few times, juking out Glendale’s defense. He drove towards the byline before firing a cross. The ball ricocheted off of a Glendale defender and snuck through the goal at the near post. “It’s definitely a top momentum of my life,” Shaw said. “Scoring a game-winner in the district championship is always fun. Run to the corner and have everyone jump in and celebrate, it was super exciting.” It wasn’t the prettiest goal, but it was a testament to Nixa’s style of play. The Eagles wanted the ball down the wings and it’s where they made the most of their chances. Nixa fired cross after cross into Glendale’s box throughout the match. The variety of crosses made it difficult for Glendale. They were sometimes pinged to the six-yard line, or they were lofted to the back post. Each cross proved that Nixa was getting closer to a goal, finally hitting the back of the net with minutes to spare. “We moved our wings up the field. We wanted to make sure we’re defensively solid, but then get up and attack,” Nixa head coach Evan Palmer said. “It puts Gavin and Spencer (Rinne), who play the wing a lot, up there where they can do their stuff because they’re fantastic on the ball.” High school football: Breaking down Springfield area district semifinal action Shaw’s goal was the difference maker. The celebrations wouldn't happen without Smith’s strong wrists. He was called into action on multiple occasions, showcasing his reflexes and stopping ability. Glendale attacked down Nixa’s left wing with 10 minutes to play. A shot was fired and Shaw needed to fully extend himself to cover the back post. It was a fantastic save, but the ball filtered to the top of the box. Glendale’s next shot rattled the bar before Nixa could clear the lines. It was one of the Falcons’ best chances of the game. “I couldn’t even tell you,” Shaw said, reliving the close call. “I freaked out. I was happy, but I tried not to get too happy. I try to stay consistent and stay in the zone, but it’s hard not to get excited.” Glendale has been Nixa’s bogey team for years. In the regular season, the Falcons won 3-2. In the district championship, Nixa got its moment to shine.

item.title: Astros superstar Yordan Alvarez is getting a little antsy about Thursday’s AL MVP reveal
item.description: Astros superstar Yordan Alvarez is getting a little antsy about Thursday’s AL MVP reveal appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Houston Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez addressed the wait for Thursday’s American League MVP announcement as he prepares for a busy awards week in Las Vegas. Alvarez is one of three finalists alongside Tampa Bay Rays third baseman Junior Caminero and Kansas City Royals shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. The winner will be revealed Thursday at 7 p.m. ET/4 p.m. PT on MLB Network. The announcement follows a season in which Alvarez hit 42 home runs and drove in 106 runs across 158 games. He also earned Players Choice recognition as the AL Outstanding Player. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) MLB.com’s Brian McTaggart shared Alvarez’s comments Monday night on X, formerly Twitter, offering a glimpse into how the Astros star slugger is handling the final days before the reveal. “The last couple of days I’ve been a little nervous. The day is getting close and it’s very exciting and a little nervous for me.” Alvarez will fly to Las Vegas on Wednesday for the MLB Awards show at The Chelsea at The Cosmopolitan. He could also receive the Edgar Martinez Outstanding Designated Hitter Award and Comeback Player of the Year honors during the event. Those presentations are separate from Thursday’s MVP announcement, giving Alvarez multiple opportunities for recognition during the week. His MVP candidacy rests on a season in which he batted .316 with a .432 on-base percentage and .601 slugging percentage. His 1.033 OPS reflected a combination of power and an ability to reach base that made him a leading candidate for the award. Alvarez led the American League in all four categories while providing the Astros with production across nearly an entire regular-season schedule. His 42 homers and 106 RBIs added to an offensive resume already recognized by his fellow players. As of Monday night, the MVP result remains unannounced, with Alvarez, Caminero, and Witt awaiting Thursday’s reveal.

item.title: Missouri requested formal SEC review into officiating after getting hosed vs. Texas
item.description: John David Mercer-USA TODAY Sports. Missouri requested formal SEC review into officiating after getting hosed vs. Texas appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Missouri has formally requested the Southeastern Conference to examine the officiating from Saturday’s controversial 34-20 loss to Texas , with athletic director Laird Veatch calling for greater accountability and transparency. Veatch announced the request in a letter to Tigers fans on Monday, acknowledging the frustration surrounding several decisions that went against Missouri . “After the game Saturday, we requested a formal review and response from the SEC regarding the officiating,” shared Veatch. “Consistent with SEC expectations, we will not make those conversations or responses public, other than that we have not received anything inconsistent with what the conference has already shared publicly.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The most disputed incident occurred in the third quarter when Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning appeared to throw an incomplete pass, but officials ruled it a fumble. The replay booth upheld the original decision, giving Texas a crucial first down. The Longhorns capitalized on that possession, scoring a game-tying touchdown three plays later before adding two more touchdowns in the second half to secure the win. Other controversial decisions included a pass interference penalty against cornerback Sione Laulea, a missed intentional grounding call on Manning and the officials overturning an early rushing touchdown by Tigers quarterback Austin Simmons. Disagreements also emerged over how downfield blocking was handled on plays behind the line of scrimmage. The defeat dropped Missouri to 6-3 overall and 3-3 in conference play, knocking the Tigers out of the AP Top 25 and potentially ending their College Football Playoff hopes. Meanwhile, Texas improved its postseason position by avoiding a third loss. Missouri will next travel to Georgia before hosting Kentucky and Oklahoma in its remaining home games. item.title: Lazy Canucks Bullied By Tocchet Hockey in Tough Loss to Flyers
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Canucks looked lazy and disinterested for 40 minutes on Monday, as Philadelphia got a much-needed win at Rogers Arena by a score of 3-1. That was a classic game of Tocchet hockey. A lot of dump-ins and board battles in a very low-event game. The Canucks lost most of those board battles, which resulted in an embarrassingly low number of scoring chances, especially in the first two periods. If there was still doubt, there is no denying it now: the Canucks are the worst NHL team by a country mile. Remember, the Canucks were facing a struggling Philadelphia team that played against the Calgary Flames last night. In the end, Philadelphia bullied the Canucks and took their lunch money, and did not even need a great effort to do it. Game Stories: Chytil and Willander Out Again, Lekkerimäki Promoted, Sportsnet+ Exclusive Game As we discussed in Monday morning’s Canucks Rundown , Filip Chytil and Tom Willander were present at morning skate, but did not play tonight. Jonathan Lekkerimäki , who has had a great start this season, was rewarded with a spot on the top line with Elias Pettersson and Brock Boeser . Jacob Quillan remained a healthy scratch in this game, which remains a head-scratcher, given his heavy style of play. His forechecking, speed, and play along the wall could have been some help this game, considering how Philadelphia plays. This was the first of nine games this season where Canucks fans could only stream the game exclusively on Sportsnet+. A controversial move by Rogers as they try to drive up subscriptions. However, Canucks fans should frankly be thanking Rogers for preventing them from watching this game. This was a very tough watch. Canucks Offense Stifled in the First Period Two minutes in, Michael Bunting attempted a pass to Christian Dvorak , but the puck got between Brendan Gallagher ‘s feet and bounced to Dvorak; then Bunting found the loose puck to open the scoring. A strange goal, but definitely a frustrating one to give up early for the Canucks. Bunting’s first in 🟠 & ⚫️! #PHIvsVAN | #LetsGoFlyers pic.twitter.com/GSojwDbfMa — Philadelphia Flyers (@NHLFlyers) November 10, 2026 The Canucks struggled with making passes, keeping puck possession, and really generating much of anything in the first 20 minutes. The offense was thoroughly suffocated by Philadelphia. Laziness Sets in During the Second Period Matvei Michkov made a great pass to Travis Konecny , who put it short-side on Meriläinen on the power play at 3:05. The Canucks have surrendered a power play goal in 16 of their 20 games this season, as the puck watching and chasing continues to be a struggle to clean up. For Michkov, he continues to make a case for Tocchet to give him more ice time, as he alluded to in his recent social media activity and comments to media on Saturday. Another power play payoff. ⚡️ #PHIvsVAN | #LetsGoFlyers pic.twitter.com/VUzMG8K26V — Philadelphia Flyers (@NHLFlyers) November 10, 2026 Once again, the Canucks

item.title: Latest Puka Nacua injury update shows WR will miss significant time for LA Rams
item.description: Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images Puka Nacua has avoided a ligament tear after latest knee injury, but the injury update is still not good for the Los Angeles Rams. Wide receiver Puka Nacua has been great to start the year for the Los Angeles Rams, recording 70 receptions for 715 yards and four touchdowns in seven games. The star had arguably his best game of the year against the Washington Commanders, going off for 150 yards and a touchdown. However, things are never straightforward in the world of football. Nacua suffered an injury on the final offensive play against the Commanders. In a game the Rams won 20-13, the price they paid was their star receiver’s health. And while the initial fears have proven to be overblown, his injury is still significant. Puka Nacua will go on to IR, after spraining ACL and PCL and suffering turf toe When Puka went down, fans feared the worst. There was discussion about whether it would be a season-ending injury, with some speculating that Nacua had torn his ligament. The team has now assessed the situation, and it is not quite that bad. On Monday, Adam Schefter revealed the details of Nacua’s ailments, and despite the slight cause for optimism, it still isn’t what Rams fans will want to hear. “Rams WR Puka Nacua is likely to be placed injured reserve due to MCL and PCL sprains, per HC Sean McVay,” the NFL insider shared on Monday evening. This means that he is likely to miss at least a month of action, and it could be more as well. With games coming against the Packers, Chiefs, and 49ers during that time, this is one of the worst stretches of the year the Rams could face without one of their main targets. The team will have to find a way to win games without him. They already appear to be in a tight race for a playoff spot. item.title: Rams’ Sean McVay regret call that led to Puka Nacua injury
item.description: Amber Searls-Imagn Images Rams’ Sean McVay regret call that led to Puka Nacua injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . This season has been a total nightmare for the Los Angeles Rams . What was supposed to be their breakout campaign has become a fight for their survival every week. One of the reasons for their struggles this season is the injuries to their key players. They’re already playing most of this season without star wide receiver Davante Adams, who’s out for an extended period. Now, the Rams will be without their other star wide receiver for at least four games. P uka Nacua is set to be placed on the IR after suffering a turf toe and knee injury in their Week 9 clash against the Washington Commanders. Nacua injured his toe on a jet sweep play, an unusual play for the star wide receiver to run. The decision to put Nacua on that play has earned a lot of negative reactions from fans. After the game, head coach Sean McVay expressed his regret about calling that play. The Rams play-caller said that he’s been debating in his head whether he did make the right play call. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I’m kicking myself about those kinds of things,” McVay said, per Adam Grosbard. “I’d be lying to you if I said I haven’t questioned the decision-making on that last play over and over.” The Rams got one of their injured stars back in Week 9 when pass-rusher Myles Garrett returned to action for the first time since Week 1. However, Los Angeles will have to navigate the next few weeks of the season without another star. The Rams’ offense has been struggling this season without one of their premier pass-catchers. Now, McVay and Matthew Stafford are trying to figure out how to keep their season alive without a top-five wide receiver in the league. The Rams face the Arizona Cardinals next week. While this should be an easy matchup on paper, Los Angeles already dropped their last game against them… and that was with a relatively healthy Rams squad. item.title: Walker Kessler celebrates Luka Doncic’s unmatched impact as a scorer and playmaker
item.description: Walker Kessler celebrates Luka Doncic’s unmatched impact as a scorer and playmaker originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After missing the Los Angeles Lakers ' game against the Detroit Pistons , Luka Doncic was back in the fold on Monday to play against the Atlanta Hawks . He led the Lakers to the win once again by being a top-tier scorer and playmaker once again. For the longest time, Doncic has been known as a top-tier offensive player. Before this game against Atlanta, Doncic was averaging over 40 points per game, but that has not hampered his ability to be a playmaker, which was even more on point on Monday night. Walker Kessler celebrates Luka Doncic's ability to dominate on offense Doncic has arguably been the most dominant player in the league this season. Of course, Victor Wembanyama will argue against that because of how he started the season as well. The Doncic dominance was on display against the Hawks , as he nearly had a triple-double. He posted 32 points, eight rebounds, 10 assists, five steals, and two blocks. It was an amazing performance that Doncic made look routine. MORE: Luka Doncic could average over 40 points per game in the 2026-27 season As one of the players who benefit the most from playing with Doncic, Kessler had another good performance. He posted a strong double-double with 21 points and 10 rebounds, which he attributed to playing with Doncic. "Even when he’s scoring 40, he’s still looking for guys. Tonight the assists worked out for him. Right now he’s the best player in the NBA. And I think he’ll be the MVP. Playing with a guy like that... He just impacts the game in every possible way," Kessler said after the Lakers' win against the Hawks . Kessler won't be the only one to have these thoughts because Doncic has cemented himself as one of the league's best players. He is the favorite to win MVP alongside Wembanyama, which will be another fun race to track. item.title: Luka Doncic ruthlessly trolls Hawks fans over franchise’s biggest mistake: ‘You could have had me’
item.description: Luka Dončić didn’t just beat the Hawks on Monday night. He reminded their fans of the biggest mistake in franchise history. And he made sure to rub it in too. During the Lakers’ 124-114 victory , Dončić engaged in a hilarious courtside exchange with Hawks fans, reminding them that Atlanta once held the keys to his basketball future before foolishly trading them away. “You all wish you would have had me. You all wish, huh?” Dončić taunted, according to a video shared on Threads by @RKessler23. “We had you,” one fan fired back. “No we don’t, I’ve never wanted you,” another insisted. Jalen Johnson of the Atlanta Hawks and Luka Doncic of the Los Angeles Lakers hug after a game on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. NBAE via Getty Images Dyson Daniels of the Atlanta Hawks and Luka Doncic of the Los Angeles Lakers hug after a game on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. NBAE via Getty Images At least one Atlanta fan was willing to admit the painful truth. “I wish we did, I do,” the fan responded. “You know you could have had me,” Dončić reminded them. “He’s right,” the person recording acknowledged through laughter. Luka Doncic was trash-talking with Atlanta Hawks fans tonight in the Lakers 124-114 victory. Here's the transcript: Luka: "You all wish you would have had me. You all wish, huh?” Fan: “We had you.” Another fan: “No we don’t, I’ve never wanted you.” Another fan: “I wish… pic.twitter.com/PM7eALuMXR — Michael J. Duarte (@michaeljduarte) November 10, 2026 The exchange reopened a wound from the 2018 NBA Draft, when Atlanta selected Dončić third overall before trading him to the Mavericks in a deal involving Trae Young. Dončić eventually led Dallas to the NBA Finals, while Young has since landed in Washington alongside former Lakers star Anthony Davis. Luka Doncic of the Los Angeles Lakers reacts after a 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks at State Farm Arena in Atlanta on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. Getty Images Monday’s performance only added insult to injury. Dončić torched the Hawks for 32 points , 10 assists, eight rebounds, five steals and two blocks, becoming the first Lakers player to record multiple games with at least 30 points, five assists, five steals and two blocks. Not even Magic Johnson or Kareem Abdul-Jabbar accomplished that twice. With Dončić leading the NBA in scoring at 40.1 points per game and Los Angeles sitting atop the standings at 10-2, his argument was difficult to dispute. Atlanta had its chance. Now, eight years later and wearing a Lakers jersey, Dončić is still making the Hawks pay for their mistake. Luka Doncic (77) of the Los Angeles Lakers handles the ball against the Atlanta Hawks on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. item.title: Oscar Piastri-Mark Webber Split: A Look at Their Partnership Over the Years
item.description: Mark Webber had been managing Oscar Piastri since 2019. (Source: MEGA) Oscar Piastri has left the management team that helped steer him into Formula 1. A statement released on behalf of the McLaren driver on Monday, after the Brazilian Grand Prix, said Piastri and the team headed by ex-F1 driver Mark Webber and Ann Neal had mutually ended their agreement. While the F1 world waits to see what the new management structure will look like, we take a look back at the partnership that came to a close in Brazil. | Oscar Piastri and Mark Webber have mutually agreed to end their management partnership. Piastri will move to a new management structure, which has yet to be confirmed. His McLaren contract runs until the end of 2028. pic.twitter.com/MvNr6I36tP — Race+ (@racepluscom) November 9, 2026 It all began in 2019, when Webber signed Piastri via JAM Sports Management, right after the Australian driver had won the Formula Renault Eurocup. The following year, Piastri would climb to the top of the Formula 3 ladder, taking the championship under Webber’s guidance. Then, in 2021, Piastri would continue with his immense success, as he became the Formula 2 champion in his rookie season. 2022 saw a tumultuous incident unfold, with Piastri being subject to a chaotic situation. While Alpine had already announced the Australian driver’s arrival at their camp for the 2023 season, Piastri would decline the move and move to McLaren instead. Webber remained a key instrument in the orchestration of the entire debacle, with the FIA ultimately ruling in favor of the Aussie. 2023 would see Piastri make his F1 debut with McLaren, replacing Daniel Ricciardo under Webber’s guidance. And in the following two years, he would earn crucial podiums and race wins to help McLaren win back-to-back constructors’ championships before ending his alliance with Webber in 2026. Why Oscar Piastri Ended His Partnership With Mark Webber While the timing of the move may have come as a surprise to most, the writing had been on the wall since February this year. Piastri had already hinted at a change in the overall setup in his management team, with Webber taking on a more behind-the-scenes approach rather than being present trackside. Mark Webber was serving a reduced trackside role for Oscar Piastri. (Source: MEGA) “Mark is still very much involved and I’ve been in contact with him a lot over the last few weeks. He just won’t be trackside as much anymore. So that’s really the extent of it. There was nothing specific that triggered it,” Piastri had said at the time. And in a statement released after the Brazil race, Webber detailed that part of the reason for the split was his reduced trackside role. While the split now gives the McLaren driver the chance to build a partnership with new management, it also allows Webber and Ann to work on new ventures of their own. Smith says he hopes that pursuit ends with a ring. The ESPN personality addressed his disagreements with James, making clear that he no longer wants to carry personal resentment. That is a different tone. Smith acknowledged the friction rather than pretending it never existed. However, he also pushed back against the idea that his criticism amounts to hatred. His message was that whatever anger he previously felt has run its course. “We all know that I’ve had my issues with LeBron James and vice versa. I do not hate the man,” Smith said. “I was pissed off at once upon a time, but I’m thoroughly over that.” Stephen A. Smith Says He Has Moved Past LeBron James Issues Smith explained his position by pointing to his age and how he wants to spend his time. At 59, he said, holding onto the disagreement no longer appeals to him. The comments framed his change in attitude as a personal decision rather than a new basketball evaluation. “I’m 59 years old. Life is short. Ain’t got time for all of that,” Smith said. “I wish him nothing but the best.” That does not mean Smith has promised to agree with James or stop criticizing his performances. Basketball analysis and personal resentment are different things. What Smith described was a willingness to leave the latter behind while continuing to cover one of the sport’s biggest names. item.title: ‘No, they do not’: Skip Bayless has something to say about LeBron James after what the Lakers did
item.description: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images Skip Bayless has aimed yet another dig at LeBron James, this time following the Los Angeles Lakers’ 124-114 win against the Atlanta Hawks. The Lakers had Luka Doncic back after he missed their last game, and he scored 32 points to help them win the game. Walker Kessler got a double-double too, and they didn’t even have Austin Reaves available. That shows just how good a side they are, and Bayless has used this to criticise James without even naming him. Skip Bayless says the Los Angeles Lakers don’t miss LeBron James James spent eight years with the Los Angeles Lakers and helped them win the 2020 NBA Championship. The King had his ups and downs with the team, but when he was at his best, he was exceptional and among the very best players the NBA had ever seen. Yet, many people like Bayless have constantly had a go at James for his shortcomings during his time with the Lakers. Even though it has been a few months since he left Los Angeles and joined the Philadelphia 76ers, some of them still fire shots at James while speaking about the Lakers. That is exactly what Bayless appears to have done now, by claiming that the Los Angeles giants don’t miss ‘him’. There is no direct mention of James, but we all know who he is talking about. He tweeted after their win against the Hawks: “The Los Angeles Lakers now have the NBA’s best record. No, they do not miss him.” That last line is unnecessary, in our opinion, but the Lakers deserve huge credit for the way they have performed in the opening 12 games of the season, winning 10. There were a few concerns when James left, and some people even felt they weren’t strong enough to compete with the big teams this season. However, the Lakers have been incredible, and even when Doncic hasn’t been available, they have looked very impressive. That shows how good they are, and even though Bayless didn’t have to say it, it does look like the Lakers are not missing ‘him’. item.title: Doncic leads Lakers past Hawks, Wemby sparks Spurs
item.description: Luka Doncic's 32 points helped the in-form Los Angeles Lakers power past the Atlanta Hawks on the road (Kevin C. Cox) Luka Doncic scored 32 points as the in-form Los Angeles Lakers rolled to a sixth straight victory with a 124-114 defeat of the Atlanta Hawks on Monday. Doncic, whose sensational early season form has propelled the Lakers to the top of the NBA Western Conference, once again led from the front to secure an impressive win on the road. The Slovenian star finished with 32 points, 10 assists, eight rebounds, five steals and two blocks in a dominant all round performance. Doncic, who is averaging 40 points per game so far this season, received offensive support from Sandro Mamukelashvili, who delivered an eye-catching 23 points from the bench that included five three-pointers. Walker Kessler added 21 points with Collin Sexton scoring 18 and Ziaire Williams 12. Lakers coach J.J. Redick paid tribute to the contributions of Doncic, Sexton and Mamukelashvili on a night when the team were missing Austin Reaves (illness) and Quentin Grimes (injury). "I thought Collin did a really nice job of giving us some juice and Sandro had his best game as a Laker," Redick said. "That was awesome. "Luka, again, just orchestrating. He was out there without a secondary ball handler so he had to be on the ball a lot and that was taxing. I thought he handled it well," Redick added. The Lakers improved to 10-2 at the top of the Western Conference following the win as Atlanta fell to 7-5. The San Antonio Spurs meanwhile maintained their hot pursuit of the Lakers in the West, extending their winning streak to nine games after blowing out the Phoenix Suns 122-96 on the road to improve to 9-2. Spurs star Victor Wembanyama – fresh from a career-high 52-point performance last week – was once again in dazzling form, dropping 40 points with 11 rebounds, eight blocks and three assists in a dominant victory. "There's a lot of good going on obviously," San Antonio coach Mitch Johnson said of Wembanyama's rich vein of recent form. "I think he's allowing the game to unfold naturally and he's doing a great job of putting himself in positions to take advantage of the opportunities that are in front of him. And his team-mates are doing a good job of utilizing him when appropriate." The Golden State Warriors kept their own winning streak alive on Monday, thrashing the New Orleans Pelicans 138-87 to record their eighth consecutive victory. Stephen Curry and Brandin Podziemski scored 23 points apiece while rookie sensation Yaxel Lendeborg added 23 as the Warriors improved to 8-3. In other games on Monday, the Detroit Pistons improved to 7-3 with a 122-111 defeat of the Washington Wizards after 24 points from John Collins. The Memphis Grizzlies are also on 7-3 after their 118-102 victory over the Toronto Raptors. The Cleveland Cavaliers meanwhile stumbled to a 124-112 loss to the Charlotte Hornets. item.title: Jordan Davis is ‘glad’ to help Eagles 1 last time in heartbreaking final message
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Jordan Davis is ‘glad’ to help Eagles 1 last time in heartbreaking final message appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After coming up short for the seventh game in a row, Jordan Davis suddenly found himself heading to a team with almost the opposite record following the Philadelphia Eagles ’ decision to trade for a 2027 first and 2029 second round pick: the Jacksonville Jaguars. On paper, the deal makes sense for both teams, as the Jaguars get better now while the Eagles get better in the future, but how does it feel for Davis, who was just named a captain earlier this year? Talking to FOX29 Philly’s Jeff Skversky at the airport, Davis noted that while he’s a little disappointed to leave the Eagles, he’s happy he can continue to help the team even in his departure . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “A little disappointed, but you know, understanding that they’re in a rebuilding process and the picks, a first-round and a second-round pick, you know, obviously helps the team,” Davis said. “And you know, I love those guys, so however I can help the team, even in my departure, I’m absolutely glad to be doing that.” “Disappointed” 💔Jordan Davis tells me in an exclusive 1-on-1 interview after being traded to the Jags he loves the Eagles & Philly will always have a special place in his heart but he understands the #Eagles are “rebuilding” More on @FOX29philly ▶️ https://t.co/7Q5pvUjXA0 pic.twitter.com/MBk4dpLEKS — Jeff Skversky (@JeffSkversky) November 10, 2026 Wow, as Emmanuel Acho perfectly put it on social media, even though the NFL is truly a business, Davis’ comments were “ sad to watch .” Though his stats have been somewhat underwhelming in 2026, especially as a pass rusher, Davis just agreed to a long-term extension with the Eagles because he viewed the team as his long-term home alongside fellow Georgia Bulldogs like Jalen Carter and Nolan Smith. Now, he’ll be teaming up with another alumni of Kirby Smart’s program, Travon Walker, for the foreseeable future, even if his Super Bowl ring will forever have an Eagles logo in the middle of it. item.title: 'No one would go 5-0 for that series to wind them up': Glenn McGrath hits back at Michael Vaughan over Ashes jibe
item.description: 'No one would go 5-0 for that series to wind them up': Glenn McGrath hits back at Michael Vaughan over Ashes jibe originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Michael Vaughan has stirred the pot ahead of a packed Test calendar. Australia greats Glenn McGrath and Jason Gillespie have hit back with a smile. England’s home Ashes record since 2000 gives this argument plenty of context. 'Just doing it to wind us up':Glenn McGrath laughs off Michael Vaughan's Ashes dig with classic '5-0' prediction comeback Australia great Glenn McGrath has laughed off former England captain Michael Vaughan’s latest Ashes provocation, and insisted that nobody would predict a 5-0 result just to wind up the opposition. The remark was a gentle dig at Vaughan, and it came from the man who made that very scoreline his personal trademark before almost every Ashes series he played. Vaughan had suggested on the Stick to Cricket ​​​​​​podcast that next summer’s home Ashes would be the easiest of the big Test assignments waiting for England. The Three Lions are due to play three Tests away against World Champions South Africa in early 2027, and a historic one-off Test against Australia in Melbourne will follow. After that, the team is set to fly to Bangladesh for two Tests in March, although the exact dates have not been announced yet. The home Ashes then arrives, with Australia coming to England for a five-Test series. Alastair Cook was left in fits of laughter, and Vaughan was forced to explain his thinking. “England plays South Africa for three, Bangladesh for two away,” Vaughan said on the Stick to Cricket Podcast. “From what I see already, I think the Aussie series next summer, the five here in the UK. I think of those three series, it (the Ashes) the easiest. “South Africa away from home, they are the best team in the world, Bangladesh in their own backyard, two Tests on dusty ones, we are not picking our best spinner… and then Australia at home. We haven’t lost against Australia here in the UK since 2001. I am not wrong. That’s the easiest of the three series." MORE: England squad for South Africa Test series 2026-27: Full team lists for SA vs ENG red-ball series Ashes series results in England since 2000: How the home record backs Vaughan’s argument Vaughan’s point about 2001 is correct, and the figures below show how England have fared at home against Australia since that defeat. The table also shows that the picture is more mixed than “unbeaten” suggests, because Australia kept the urn after the last two drawn series. item.title: 'Haven’t paid much attention': Mitchell Starc denies Usman Khawaja's allegation that bowlers were aware of sandpaper use in 2018
item.description: 'Haven’t paid much attention': Mitchell Starc denies Usman Khawaja's allegation that bowlers were aware of sandpaper use in 2018 originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Australia pace star Mitchell Starc has repeated his version of events from Sandpapergate. Usman Khawaja's autobiography has revived one of cricket’s most painful and divisive scandals. In a latest video, Khawaja has responded to critics who questioned his motives for telling the story. Did Australian bowlers know about Sandpapergate? Mitchell Starc responds to Usman Khawaja Mitchell Starc has made it clear that the Australian bowlers weren’t aware of any sandpaper plan in 2018, and he has no intention of changing that account now. The left-arm quick was responding to Usman Khawaja’s autobiography, which claims that every member of the touring team knew what was being planned during the Cape Town Test. Starc was speaking at the Kayo Sports and Fox Cricket season launch, where he was asked about the claims. He did not hide the fact that he had paid little attention to the debate, but he was firm on the one point that matters to him, which is that his memory of the events has not shifted in the slightest. The background to his stance is a joint statement released in 2021, after Cameron Bancroft gave an interview to The Guardian that raised fresh doubts about the official version of events. Starc, along with Nathan Lyon, Josh Hazlewood and Pat Cummins, said at the time that none of the four bowlers had known about the use of sandpaper on the ball. However, Khawaja's book has now contradicted that statement, and it has pushed an old controversy back into the headlines. “Yeah, that’s the first I was aware of any of that taking place in PE (second Test) was when (Khawaja said it) … I’ll leave that for said authors to explain,” Starc said. He went on to admit that he had not followed the discussion closely, and he pointed out that opinions from eight years ago were bound to differ. “I haven’t really paid much attention to be fair, obviously there’s differing opinions of eight years ago," he said. "We were heavily drilled through the process at the time, and since and I guess I won’t speak on behalf of the bowlers, but where I stand, my opinion hasn’t changed. My recollection hasn’t changed from what we said in 2021." His final remarks drew a narrow line around what the joint statement actually covered, which was the question of whether the bowlers knew anything was being taken onto the field. “As far as our statement said, we weren’t aware of things being taken on the field, that’s where I’ll leave it.” More to follow...

item.title: Chris Kyriacou wins Chronicle's inaugural John Beam Community Action Award
item.description: Chris Kyriacou divides players into groups during practice for the Oakland Wildcats travel baseball team on Thursday at Raimondi Park in Oakland. Kyriacou is the first recipient of the Chronicle's John Beam Community Action Award, named after the Laney College football coach who died in 2025. (Don Feria/For the S.F. Chronicle) The winner of the Chronicle's inaugural John Beam Community Action Award is Chris Kyriacou, a physical education teacher at Bishop O'Dowd High School and the coach of the Oakland Wildcats, a youth travel baseball team. Kyriacou, 61, has had an indelible impact on the Oakland community through four decades as a coach, educator and leader - just like Beam, the legendary former Skyline High and Laney College coach and athletic director who died last November. Kyriacou described Beam as a big brother, a mentor, a friend and a colleague all wrapped in one. Beam and Kyriacou grew up together in the Oakland high school sports scene, and although they spent only seven years on the same staff at Skyline High, the pair worked hand-in-hand to shape countless lives over almost 40 years. Kyriacou has taught and coached at Skyline, San Lorenzo and Bishop O'Dowd, where he has spent the past two-plus decades. "Coach was so many things to me and many people in Oakland. Not just players - other students, other adults," Kyriacou said. "Coach was just invaluable." Beam called Kyriacou "one of my best friends" when they attended the Athletics' final home game together in 2024. Kyriacou gave a touching tribute to Beam at his celebration of life in January. To understand the full relationship between these two fiery personalities, however, it's best to start at the beginning, when things started off on not so great terms. Oakland teacher and coach Chris Kyriacou speaks during a celebration of life for John Beam on Jan. 10 at the Henry J. Kaiser Center for the Arts in Oakland. (Carlos Avila Gonzalez/S.F. Chronicle) "Sadly," Kyriacou said, "our first encounter with each other was yelling at each other." Kyriacou was a senior at Oakland High. Beam was a 23-year-old first-year defensive coordinator at Skyline. Their football teams were facing off in a heated rivalry game. After Kyriacou made a tackle on an Oakland High player near the sideline, he began "talking some crap." "(Beam's) going, ‘Hey, man, get out of here! You ain't doing nothing!'" item.title: Victor Wembanyama joins Shaq in NBA history
item.description: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Victor Wembanyama joins Shaq in NBA history appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Antonio Spurs have gotten their season off to a strong start, and a big reason for that is their big man out of France. Led by Victor Wembanyama, the Spurs have won eight of their first 10 games to start the 2026-27 regular season, and lead the Phoenix Suns by 15 at the half on Monday night. Through his first 10 games played this season, Victor Wembanyama is averaging 29.1 points, 12.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.2 steals, and 3.9 blocks per game while shooting 50.5 percent from the field. It’s an absurd start to a season by the fourth year center. In fact, it’s so good that is actually joined the history books. With those first-half numbers, Victor Wembanyama joined Basketball Hall-of-Famer Shaquille O’Neal as the only players in the last 50 seasons to average 29 points, 12 rebounds, and three blocked shots through the first 10 games of a season. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) O’Neal was the only other player to complete the feat, averaging 29.2 points, 12.2 rebounds, and 3.0 blocks per game to start the 2001-02 season with the Los Angeles Lakers. In the first half on Monday, Wembanyama recorded 22 points and five blocks, just the 13th time in NBA history that the statline has been recorded in a single half. What’s crazier is that this is the second time in the last week that Wembanyama has done this. The Spurs went on to win the game, with Wembanyama going on to finish with 40 points, 11 rebounds, and eight blocked shots. It’s the second time he’s recorded a 40-point, 10-rebound game this season. The rest of the NBA has done that twice this season. Related: Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama takes off from behind the FT line for insane finish

item.description: ‘She’s Going To Have To Talk About (Mike) Vrabel’ — Analyst Warns Dianna Russini Must ‘Address’ Allegations About Controversy Involving Patriots HC Dianna Russini is getting another shot at a career in sports media, but not everyone is ready to move on from how her last stint ended. On Monday, the offshore sportsbook BetUS announced that Russini will host a weekly live show, “The Russini Report,” debuting Wednesday at noon ET. Her first interview since resigning from The Athletic offered some insight into the difficult months she has endured, but said little about the Mike Vrabel situation that brought her under scrutiny. Radio host Jared Stillman thinks that will become a problem for Russini soon. What Dianna Russini Said and Left Out Before Her BetUS Debut Russini’s new venture will give her a weekly platform to discuss football. “The Russini Report” will run for an hour on BetUS TV, previewing games for bettors, breaking down matchups, and featuring guests. She will also write a weekly column as part of the partnership. People magazine published her first interview since she resigned from her NFL insider role in April, days after photos of her with New England Patriots head coach Vrabel at an Arizona resort surfaced. Looking back on everything that followed the photos, Russini told People, “The best way to describe what the last six months were like for me is heartbreaking.” She and Vrabel, each married to someone else, had both described the relationship as platonic in statements when the photos surfaced, and in the interview she never mentioned him by name. Why Jared Stillman Thinks Dianna Russini Has to Address Mike Vrabel Scandal Stillman, who hosts “Stillman and Company,” laid out the stakes in a video he posted on X ahead of the premiere of Russini’s show. “In order for her to be taken seriously, she’s going to have to talk about Vrabel again,” he said.
