item.title: US-mediated talks with Russia and Ukraine to start in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States will hold talks in Abu Dhabi Tuesday on ending Europe’s worst conflict since World War II in the first such meeting in more than nine months, as another winter of war approaches. Europe – alarmed by US President Donald Trump floating a deal with Moscow on European security ahead of the talks – will also send representatives to Abu Dhabi. Trump has pushed for an end to the Russia-Ukraine war since returning to power, but previous talks produced no breakthroughs and the process became sidelined by the US-Israeli war against Iran. Europe and Ukraine fear the United States will force a deal on Kyiv that would amount to a de-facto capitulation, with Trump appearing to pivot towards Moscow this year. Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine has killed hundreds of thousands, displaced millions and has dragged on for 56 months, with the Kremlin showing no sign of backing down. Trump hinted Ukraine will have to give up land ahead of the talks, saying: “They’re going to end up with a little bit different shape, Ukraine.” Russia occupies large swathes of Ukraine but, while its troops have grinded westwards, they have not been able to seize the whole of the Donetsk region. Moscow demands Kyiv surrender the parts of the region it still controls, vowing it will otherwise press on with its offensive. Ukraine – which for more than 4.5 years has resisted a far larger invading army at a huge human cost – has ruled out such a withdrawal. Russia pummelled Ukraine in the run-up to the talks and carried out one of its deadliest strikes yet – with Kyiv saying 55 people were killed in a frontline village as they queued for humanitarian aid. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the intensified strikes were part of Moscow’s strategy of “putting pressure on Ukraine’s position” at the negotiations. Russia’s Vladimir Putin, who launched the war in February 2022, has repeatedly refused broader ceasefire offers and face-to-face talks with Zelensky. Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff will gather the enemy sides in Abu Dhabi for the first time since February, when negotiations took place in Geneva. Russia and Ukraine have held several rounds of failed talks during almost five years of war and hopes for peace are low. “We don’t have any particular expectations,” a senior Ukrainian official in Kyiv told AFP. ‘We don’t want Yalta 2.0’ Trump last week floated a “very big agreement” on the war that will “involve all of Europe”, stoking fears Washington would collaborate with Moscow on creating a new European security architecture. Shortly before launching its 2022 invasion, Moscow had issued an ultimatum to the West for NATO to rollback troops from Eastern Europe. The diplomat who issued the demand, Sergei Ryabkov, will for the first time be part of Moscow’s delegation, which is headed by Putin’s nationalistic aide Vladimir Medinsky. item.title: Rivers community that forbids female dogs explains tradition to NYSC members
item.description: By Davies Iheamnachor — APARA The people of Ekinobo in Apara Kingdom, Ikwerre ethnic nationality of Rivers State, have raised the alarm over the growing disregard for their customs, including a longstanding prohibition against keeping female dogs in the community. •His Royal Majesty Eze Ohna Apara Kingdom, Gift Eziwhuo Johnson (middle), flanked by corps members. The community, located in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area, said urbanization, the influx of strangers and increasing Western influence had contributed to the erosion of its cultural heritage and traditional practices. This came as the Paramount Ruler of Apara Kingdom, His Royal Majesty, Eze Gift Eziwhuo Johnson, Eze Ohna Apara IV, and the Chiefs-in-Council hosted members of the Culture and Tourism Community Development Service (CDS) of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) to a cultural orientation programme on the customs, traditions and laws of the Apara people. The corps members embarked on the visit as part of an initiative to familiarise themselves with the cultural values of their host communities, understand local traditions and avoid practices capable of offending indigenous sensibilities. The visit also provided an opportunity for the traditional institution to seek stronger collaboration with the NYSC in promoting mutual understanding, preserving cultural heritage and fostering peaceful relationships. NYSC members visit Speaking during the visit, the leader of the Culture and Tourism CDS group, Dominic Umoh, said the initiative was designed to expose corps members to the cultural values of their host communities and preserve such knowledge for future generations. He explained that understanding local customs was important because corps members could eventually establish personal and family relationships with people from their places of service. “We might get married to somebody from here, so there is a need for us to understand their culture. We are here to know the dos and don’ts of the Ikwerre people,” he said. Lectures on Iwhuruoha, popularly known as Ikwerre, culture and traditions were delivered by Eze (Dr) Chibuike Wali, Darlington Wigwe, Prof. Nmecha Akani and Chief (Dr) Chinedu Amadi. Commending the corps members, Eze Johnson, who spoke through the Palace Spokesman, Chief Chinedu Amadi, described the engagement as worthwhile and successful, noting that chiefs from different parts of Apara Kingdom attended to demonstrate their support. He said the corps members were educated on several traditional practices, including the prohibition against female dogs and traditional rites associated with deaths occurring on certain days, particularly a day locally known as Iriagbo. “We were able to tell them certain things or certain cultures that are permissible in this part of the world. One of the lecturers said female dogs are not allowed in this place. There is also a particular day that if somebody dies, it is taboo. That day we call Iriagbo,” he said. The monarch stressed tha

item.title: I won’t surrender my senatorial ticket — Uzodimma
item.description: Governor Hope Uzodimma of Imo State has insisted that he remains in the 2027 Senatorial race, describing suggestions that he would surrender his ambition to another candidate as “a lie”. Read Also: Court sacks Uzodinma as APC senatorial candidate for Imo West A Federal High Court sitting in Abuja, on October 29, 2026, ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to remove Uzodimma’s name as Senatorial candidate for Imo West and replace it with the name of former Governor Rochas Okorocha. Justice Obiora Egwuatu based the judgment on the grounds that Uzodimma did not win the All Progressives Congress, APC, primary election held on May 18. The outcome of the ruling has since been rejected by the APC in the state, with the party insisting that Uzodimma remains its candidate for Imo West Senatorial District. Speaking on Sunday after attending Mass at the Government House Chapel in Owerri, the Imo state capital, Uzodimma dismissed insinuations that he would cede his ticket to anyone as deceptive. “If they tell you that I will hold this ticket and somebody will collect it and give it to another, tell the person it is a lie,” he said. He called on residents of the state to canvass support for the APC to ensure its victory across all levels, mentioning names of candidates voters should rally round in the forthcoming elections. “Go and campaign for the party, our great party, the All Progressives Congress, APC. There is no other political party we are going with. “For the House of Assembly, it is APC. For the House of Representatives, it is APC,” the governor said. He added, “For the Senate, your senator in Okigwe zone is Patrick Ndubueze, in Orlu zone it is my humble self (Hope Uzodimma), and in Owerri zone it is (Alex) Mbata,” he said. Okorocha Meanwhile, Okorocha had earlier described the ruling nullifying Uzodimma’s candidacy as a victory for the nation’s judiciary and democracy. Okorocha, in a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Media, Sam Onwuemodo, commended President Bola Tinubu for, according to him, providing the enabling environment for the Judiciary and other Institutions to function for the nation’s rapid development and growth. “This judgment, to say the least, is a resounding victory for the nation’s judiciary. It is a victory for the nation’s fast-growing democracy. It is an outstanding victory for the nation’s Constitution, as amended. He added, “It is a remarkable victory for all lovers of what is right and haters of what is wrong. It is a notable victory for posterity and history. “Finally, it is a victory for Imo people in general, and Imo West Senatorial District people in particular.” Vanguard News The post I won’t surrender my senatorial ticket — Uzodimma appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 10 – Saturn Behind the Moon
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 10 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Saturn Behind the Moon Explanation: Sometimes Saturn disappears. It doesn’t really go away, of course — it just disappears from our view when Earth’s Moon moves in front. Such a Saturn ian eclipse, more formally called an occultation , was visible in early 2025 along a small swath of Earth — from Greenland through central Europe and into northern Africa . The featured image is a digital fusion of three images, the first of just Saturn before it disappeared, and then two more of the Moon with different exposure lengths. The images were taken from Sardinia , Italy , after sunset. The bright dot near Saturn is not a moon of Saturn , but rather the star 85 Aquarii , which is further behind Saturn than Saturn is behind the Moon. The next time the Moon moves in front of Saturn, as visible from some place on Earth , will be in 2031. Tomorrow’s picture: small but mighty Date November 10, 2026 Credit & Copyright Roberto Ortu Authors & editors: Robert Nemiroff, Jerry Bonnell, Cecilia Chirenti, Keighley Rockcliffe A service of: ASD at NASA / GSFC , NASA Science Activation & Michigan Tech. item.title: Autumn Mornings Bring Valley Fog
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Autumn Mornings Bring Valley Fog Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search morning afternoon A natural-color satellite image from the morning shows white fog filling a branching network of river valleys, surrounded by brown and green terrain. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin A false-color satellite image from the afternoon shows the same area clear of fog, with rivers and lakes in dark blue winding through bright green vegetation. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin morning afternoon A natural-color satellite image from the morning shows white fog filling a branching network of river valleys, surrounded by brown and green terrain. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin A false-color satellite image from the afternoon shows the same area clear of fog, with rivers and lakes in dark blue winding through bright green vegetation. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin morning afternoon Curtain Toggle 2-Up Image Details On November 8, 2026, low clouds traced the branching valleys of the Appalachian Plateau and the Cumberland River in the morning (left, natural color) then burned off by afternoon (right, false color). The images were acquired with the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) on NASA’s Terra satellite and the VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) on NOAA-21 , respectively. NASA Earth Observatory images by Lauren Dauphin. On a cool November morning, low clouds traced the branching valleys of the Appalachian Plateau and the Cumberland River. By afternoon, they had faded, leaving clear skies over the autumn landscape. The change is visible in this pair of images from November 8, 2026. The MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) on NASA’s Terra satellite acquired the left image that morning. In this natural-color view, low clouds appear white as they fill many of the valleys. Autumn vegetation appears in shades of brown and green. The VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) on NOAA-21 acquired the right image that afternoon, after the clouds had dissipated and exposed the rivers and lakes beneath them. This false-color view makes it easier to distinguish water (dark blue) from vegetation (bright green). The clouds appear to be fog, a type of cloud that forms near the ground . Foggy mornings in the region are common this time of year. As nights lengthen, the ground has more time to radiate away the day’s heat, and the air just above it cools to the dew point —the temperature at which air becomes saturated and water vapor begins condensing into the tiny droplets that make up fog. item.title: Explainer: Election results collation chain that decides Nigeria’s president
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – Nigeria’s president is not declared on the strength of a single national count. A chain of collation officers, each signing for the votes below them, builds the result from the polling unit up to the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC. Read Also: * Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal * Why getting most votes is not enough to become Nigeria’s president The chain starts when voting ends. Voters are accredited with the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, and the presiding officer counts the ballots in public and enters each party’s score on Form EC8A, the polling unit result sheet. The presiding officer signs the form, and polling agents who are present countersign it. A poster version, Form EC60E, is pasted at the polling unit so voters can see what was recorded. Collation then moves upward. INEC’s then chairman, Mahmood Yakubu, described the 2023 process as running through “four levels”: ward, local government area, LGA, state and national. At each level, an officer adds up the forms from the level below and records the total on a new form. The election results forms The ward collation officer adds up the Form EC8A sheets in the ward and records the total on Form EC8B. The LGA collation officer then adds up the ward sheets on Form EC8C. At state level, the State Collation Officer for the Presidential Election (SCOPE) adds up the LGA results on Form EC8D. Katsina in 2023 shows what that form contains: 3,516,719 registered voters; 1,097,663 accredited; 1,058,673 valid votes, and 32,514 rejected. Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, led with 489,045 votes against 482,283 for Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC. The national stage takes place in Abuja, with the INEC Chairman acting as returning officer for the presidential election. That office is now held by Joash Amupitan, who succeeded Yakubu in October 2025. In 2023, Yakubu set out the procedure at the national collation centre, where each state’s SCOPE presents the original Form EC8D. “When all the SCOPES have presented their results,” the returning officer displays the sealed copies of Form EC8DA, the state-by-state summary, and Form EC8E, the declaration sheet. Polling agents are invited to comment before the winner is declared, and each agent receives duplicate copies afterwards. Declaring winner Declaring the winner involves more than adding up votes. The returning officer must also confirm that the candidate with the highest total reached one-quarter of the votes in enough states, as Section 134 of the Constitution requires. The 2023 totals show the arithmetic. Yakubu put registered voters at 93,469,008; accredited voters at 25,286,616; valid votes at 24,025,940, and rejected votes at 939,278. Tinubu polled 8,794,726; Atiku 6,984,520; Peter Obi of the Labour Party, LP, 6,101,533, and Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party, NNPP, 1,496,687. On the spread test, Tinubu’s lawyer

item.title: Power outages remain despite rise in generation, ministerial promise
item.description: By Udeme Akpan, Ediri Ejoh, Obas Esiedesa & Cynthia Alo Nigeria’s electricity generation rose to 4,020.41 megawatts (MW) on Monday from 3,500MW, but the increase has yet to translate into adequate supply for consumers across the country. This comes as the promise last Thursday by the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, to restore normalcy in power supply within 72 hours expired two days ago. Data obtained from the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) showed that 20 power plants were connected to the national grid as of 1.0pm yesterday, producing a combined 4,020.41MW. The output was below Sunday’s peak generation of 4,253.6MW but above the off-peak figure of 3,862.17MW. Last Thursday, generation had dropped to 3,659MW from 3,996MW recorded the previous day, worsening supply conditions across several parts of the country. Promising restoration within 72 hours, the Ministry of Power had ruled out a major or systemic national grid failure, explaining that preliminary assessments linked the disruptions to maintenance and operational challenges across parts of the power value chain, alongside declining generation. An analysis of Monday’s generation profile showed that Afam VI contributed the highest output of 519MW, followed by Shiroro Hydro Power Plant with 445MW and Azura-Edo Independent Power Plant with 438MW. Egbin Power Plant, with an installed capacity of 1,320MW, contributed 108MW. Meanwhile, load allocation to the 11 electricity distribution companies (DisCos) stood at a combined 3,195MW as of 5:07pm yesterday; Abuja DisCo received 581MW; Ikeja 467MW; Eko 458MW and Ibadan 359MW. Others were Port Harcourt, 294MW; Benin, 243MW; Enugu, 233MW; Kano, 173MW; Kaduna, 167MW; Jos, 146MW; and Yola, 74MW. In his update on the power situation, Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, said electricity had been restored to many communities affected by recent disruptions, particularly in Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Kwara and the Federal Capital Territory. He disclosed that the vandalised Benin-Egbin 330kV transmission line had been repaired and returned to service, helping to raise electricity supply to the Lagos Complex to more than 1,000MW. However, he acknowledged that some locations were still experiencing outages. “Our priority continues to be the provision of reliable electricity to Nigerians,” he said. Speaking on a TVC programme monitored by Vanguard, Tegbe said: “Let me start by telling Nigerians, especially those in the three or four states that were recently affected by the outage, that I feel their pain, and President Bola Tinubu feels your pain. However, we are doing the best we can, and I believe it will get better.” He disclosed that the Federal Government had paid N1.23 trillion out of the N3.3 trillion owed to generation companies (GenCos), leaving about N2 trillion outstanding, which it hoped to settle next year. item.title: 2027: Tinubu’s projects’ll transform South-East economy – Shettima
item.description: *Yari demands 1.2m votes from Ebonyi; Umahi promises 1.3m *‘If Tinubu isn’t re-elected, ongoing projects’ll stop’ — Uzodimma *APC has built Nigeria for benefit of few — Makinde *PRP accuses APC of suffocating opposition, exploiting religious fault lines By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Omeiza Ajayi, Ndahi Marama & Luminous Jannamike Vice President Kashim Shettima has said President Bola Tinubu’s massive investments in security, infrastructure, agriculture and human capital development are transforming the South-East economy, promising to address the region’s longstanding development challenges. Shettima, who spoke yesterday at the All Progressives Congress, APC, presidential campaign rally in Abakaliki, Ebonyi State, said the Federal Government’s interventions were aimed at improving connectivity, strengthening food security, expanding economic opportunities and restoring security. He said the administration had demonstrated its commitment to Ebonyi through major infrastructure projects, federal appointments and welfare programmes. “This campaign has been a season of triumph. We have triumphed over the falsehoods of our opponents. We have never turned our backs on you. We have answered your support with projects, and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has honoured Ebonyi through distinguished appointments and projects across the state,” he said. According to him, Ebonyi has benefited from the dividends of democracy and deserves to renew the President’s mandate. “You have stood by us. You have assured us that a mandate is a debt of honour, repayable only through service. Yet democracy demands the humility of asking again. We have returned to seek the renewal of your mandate, to serve you, defend you and stand by you,” he added. Listing the Federal Government’s infrastructure projects, Shettima identified the Calabar–Ebonyi–Benue–Kogi–Nasarawa–Abuja Superhighway, part of the administration’s Trans-Saharan highway vision, as a major initiative to strengthen trade between the South-East, North-Central and other regions. Others are the Ndibe Bridge, which will link Ebonyi with Cross River State; the Enugu–Abakaliki–Ogoja Expressway; and the Okposi–Ohaozara–Ukawu–Cross River road. He said the projects would ease the transportation of agricultural produce and manufactured goods, improve market access and reduce business costs. On agriculture, the Vice President described Ebonyi as a major contributor to national food security through rice and cassava production. He listed fertiliser distribution, interest-free FarmerMoni assistance and rural road investments among measures to support farmers. He also disclosed that thousands of Ebonyi residents had benefited from grants under the Presidential Conditional Grant Scheme, while federal employment and digital skills programmes were creating opportunities for youths. item.title: Flamingos: Presidency, Obi bicker over access to players at Abuja airport
item.description: *NFF officials stopped me from greeting Flamingos, Obi *Don’t politicise sports, Presidency tells NDC *Keyamo accuses him of hypocrisy By Henry Umoru ABUJA—THE Media Office of the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, alleged yesterday he was stopped by officials of the Nigeria Football Federation, NFF, from greeting the victorious women’s Under-17 World Champions at Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, on arrival of the team from Morocco, venue of the tournament. Read Also: U-17 WWC: How we overcame opening defeat to win title – Oluebube The Presidency in a swift reaction, faulted the NDC presidential candidate’s claim, even as the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, accused him of hypocrisy. But in a statement signed by spokesperson of Peter Obi Media Office, POMO, Idris Zekeri , the office said the former Anambra State governor was at the airport on his way to Enugu and saw the team that had just arrived. It explained that as Obi tried to greet the players, officials of the NFF pleaded with him to save their jobs. The Media Office said in his usual character, Obi respected their position but described the situation on his X handle as a new dimension of toxic politics in Nigeria. Quoting the NDC presidential hopeful, the statement read: ‘’This is the new dimension of toxic politics that Nigeria has developed since 2025. “I arrived at the airport at 7 a.m. this morning (yesterday) to board my flight to Enugu. There, I saw the Nigeria Under-17 girls’ team, which had just arrived and was preparing to board its vehicle into town. “With genuine joy and enthusiasm, I asked my protocol officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether I could greet and welcome the team. I was informed that officials of the Nigerian Football Federation, NFF, had refused and had requested that I should not approach them because, if I did, they would all lose their jobs. “Regrettably, this is not the first time I have been subjected to such treatment. On March 25, 2025, I was in Uyo for the World Cup qualifier. The governor warmly received me and welcomed me at the VIP stand. ‘’Following the match, other government officials went to greet the players, but I was again prevented from doing so. I was told by the officials that they would lose their jobs if I proceeded. “It is deeply troubling to witness the extent of toxic politics into which our nation has descended since 2025. Each year appears to bring further deterioration. This reflects how deeply Nigeria has been affected. “The new Nigeria we aspire to build must have no room for hostility, intimidation or discrimination, regardless of political affiliation. It must be a Nigeria in which unity, mutual respect and our shared humanity take precedence over political differences. A new Nigeria is possible.” Don’t politicise sports, Presidency tells Obi over Flamingos greeting Replying Obi, the Presidency in a statement by the Special Assistant to the Pre

item.title: Cisco to link all future products to its SaaS-y Cloud Control management tool
item.description: Cisco will no longer create products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control, its SaaS-y management platform that offers netadmins a single tool to manage all of the networking giant’s devices and much of its software portfolio. The networking giant announced Cloud Control in June 2025 and only made it available to customers in the USA. Cisco has previously told The Register that slow rollout reflects the fact that Cisco needs to nail privacy and other regulatory niceties, and deploy infrastructure, before introducing the service to other markets. It appears Cisco is now satisfied it has sorted out those issues. Jeff Schultz, Cisco’s senior vice president for portfolio strategy and marketing, today told the company’s Live conference in Australia that Cloud Control will come online in the European Union, UK, and Down Under in February 2027. Japan, India, and Canada will get their turn in May. Schultz said Cisco is “working tirelessly” to deploy Cloud Control across the world as soon as possible. He also revealed that, starting next year, Cisco will no longer ship products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control. That doesn’t mean those products will be manageable only if they can connect to Cloud Control. Instead, the decision reflects Cisco’s belief that the main thing stopping its customers buying more of its products is the complexity of operating them in concert. Schultz also feels that Cloud Control represents “platform advantage” for Cisco, because when users integrate networking, security, and observability the result is better manageability and resilience. Schultz also told the conference that Cisco will bundle its Thousand Eyes observability and security tool with the “Essentials” and “Advantage” licenses. “We admit it was hard to license and deploy,” he said during his keynote speech, adding that the tool will be deployed automatically with Wi‑Fi 6E and Wi‑Fi 7 hardware. Another product Cisco plans to bring to more customers is Live Protect, a tool that implements compensating controls for flaws that organizations can’t immediately patch. The product has become particularly useful since Anthropic's Mythos model, and similar AI offerings, made it possible to quickly find more software bugs and flaws and overwhelmed tech teams whose patching apparatus was not set up to handle hundreds of montly CVEs. Live Protect currently works on some of Cisco's datacenter switches, plus SD-WAN and WLAN controllers. From December, Cisco will extend it to 8000 series routers, secure firewalls, campus gateway, and to Cloud Control itself. From May 2027, Live Protect will work with Cisco’s ASR 9000 series service aggregation routers and Network Convergence System. "Expect this to be a major investment area," Schultz added. ®

item.title: INEC and voter register crisis
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has removed 1,608,660 invalid voter registrations from the preliminary voters register and identified 54 staff members across 10 states for disciplinary action, including possible prosecution, over their alleged involvement in registration irregularities. The commission also removed 873 records belonging to verified deceased persons following complaints and objections raised during the display of the preliminary voters register ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, disclosed this on Monday in Abuja while briefing journalists on the outcome of the commission’s review of the preliminary register, describing the exercise as part of efforts to strengthen the credibility and integrity of the electoral process. The integrity of the voter register has come under fresh scrutiny following allegations of artificial intelligence (AI)-generated photographs, duplicate registrations and fictitious voter identities in the preliminary register released by INEC ahead of the 2027 general elections. The controversy sparked widespread reactions after images of questionable voter records circulated on social media, prompting calls for an investigation and greater transparency from the commission. Addressing journalists on Monday, Amupitan said the commission had concluded the cleaning exercise covering the 2025/2026 Continuous Voter Registration (CVR), adding that all confirmed invalid registrations identified through biometric screening and public complaints had been removed. According to him, the commission harvested 11,088,238 registration records from the three phases of the CVR exercise, out of which its Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) initially flagged 1,545,052 for further examination. He explained that 1,277,052 registrations were confirmed invalid and excluded before the publication of the preliminary register. The INEC chairman said following the subsequent display of the register between October 9 and 15, the commission received complaints, claims and objections from members of the public, prompting further investigations. He said 268,000 cases were subjected to adjudication, out of which 217,722 were confirmed invalid and removed, while 50,278 were cleared as valid and retained. He noted that additional screening identified another 113,886 invalid registrations, bringing the total number of invalid records removed after the review to 331,608. The INEC chairman said the commission’s investigation also uncovered deliberate attempts by some registration personnel to circumvent established procedures and misuse provisions designed for exceptional registration circumstances, including those involving persons with disabilities. He said the affected records had been identified and subjected to appropriate corrective measures, while the personnel implicated had been identified for administrative investigation. “Fifty-four persons cutting across 10 states have

item.title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 5056-5062: Charging Back Up!
item.description: Curiosity Navigation Curiosity Home Mission Overview Where is Curiosity? Mission Updates Science Overview Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Curiosity Raw Images Images Videos Audio Mosaics More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home 3 min read Curiosity Blog, Sols 5056-5062: Charging Back Up! This image was taken by Right Navigation Camera onboard NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity on Sol 5062 (2026-11-02 05:40:15 UTC). NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS By Remington Free, Operations Systems Engineer, NASA-JPL Earth planning date: Friday, Oct. 30, 2026 Today’s plan covered 3 sols, 5060, 5061, and 5062, as we take a few recharging sols before getting back to our normal drilling activities. As you may know if you have been following the blog closely, we are in the middle of a drilling campaign on our target called “Nazca.” We’ve already drilled the hole, characterized the tailings from the drill hole with ChemCam, and have now done several sample dropoffs, both to our SAM and CheMin instruments within the belly of the rover. We still have a number of activities left to do as part of the campaign, including another dropoff to SAM for a different kind of analysis, and drilling cleanup activities. One of those activities is called “RAGE” (Rotate to Agitate for Granule Expulsion, a very fun acronym) where we essentially shake the drill to get any remaining sample out of it. We’ll also make sure to take lots of imaging to continue document the drill hole and tailings. In any case, those activities are very power-hungry for our rover! So today’s plan purposefully did not have a lot of activities in it so we could get a nice few power positive sols before we get back to drilling. Each of our three sols had a standard morning science block, with an extra exciting brand-new activity on 5061 (more on that shortly!). Over the three sols, we conducted remote science with ChemCam active and Remote Micro-Imager mosaics on some interesting targets (“Titicaca,” “Pampas,” and “Salta”), some Mastcam imaging of our calibration target and our drill target, several Navcam dust devil studies and Mastcam tau observations, and twilight imaging. Despite this plan being recharging/waiting, we got in lots of exciting science to continue to study the Nazca crystal formations and the nearby layered rocks and bedrock. On 5061, we also conducted a brand-new engineering activity to test parallelism over one of our downlink communications windows. As the rover gets older and our power output slowly decreases over the length of the mission, we are continuously looking for new ways to execute activities with less power use. One of our strategies is parallelism – having two activities execute at the same time will save power due to the rover being awake for less time. However, we need to vet pairs of activities ahead of time to ensure they are safe to run together. This

item.title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 5050-5055: It’s Nazca, Our 49th Drill Hole
item.description: Curiosity Navigation Curiosity Home Mission Overview Where is Curiosity? Mission Updates Science Overview Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Curiosity Raw Images Images Videos Audio Mosaics More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home 3 min read Curiosity Blog, Sols 5050-5055: It’s Nazca, Our 49th Drill Hole This image of the Nazca drill hole was taken by Mast Camera (Mastcam) onboard NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity on Sol 5050 (2026-10-20 23:56:20 UTC). NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS Written by Susanne P. Schwenzer, Professor of Planetary Mineralogy at The Open University, UK Earth planning date: Friday, Oct. 23, 2026 As regular readers of this blog will know, we returned to the area where we found disc shaped inclusions in the rocks, which we interpreted as potential crystals. If they are indeed crystals, and we compare them to Earth, they could be very interesting indicators of the environmental conditions. Hence, the excitement in the team is high that we found a good block to drill. Good means first and foremost that it contains abundant potential crystals, but of course there is more before we drill. We passed the rover’s stability test, as all wheels have to be on solid ground before we extend the arm. Then we passed the preload test, which tests the stability of the rock and the forces the arm experiences when the drill bit presses into the rock. With all those tests passed, we successfully drilled our 49th drill hole, called “Nazca.” The drill campaign comes with many investigations before and after the drilling itself. Before the drill, we investigated the block with APXS, MAHLI and ChemCam – all on the target Nazca. After drilling, the sample was dropped off to CheMin, with the results still making their way from Mars to Earth. They are eagerly anticipated to reach us over the coming weekend. ChemCam obtained both passive spectral and active LIBS of the tailings and a LIBS measurement down the drill hole wall. Other ChemCam activities this week included a LIBS investigation of “Palpala,” which is a dark pebble. We are on the lookout for those pebbles for a while and find that not all of them have the same composition. To make sure we understand their origin, we are measuring them when there are some in reach that are big enough. If a pebble is too small, it can move when it is being hit by the laser. Hence, we need to look out for some that are big enough. Another such pebble was the target “Puna” identified in Friday’s planning. ChemCam LIBS on the target “Llama” is to get another depth profile to check whether our observations in the first such depth profile are consistently observed or whether they vary between locations. The target “Pacaya” is another measurement of the disc shaped forms that drew us back to this region. In addition to the LIBS measurements, ChemCam has several long distance RMIs in the plan. The

item.title: Global carbon emissions set to fall in 2026 due to Iran energy shock
item.description: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz led to a spike in oil prices Anna Ivanova/Alamy Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are expected to drop this year for the first time in five years. The slowdown has been partly attributed to the energy shock triggered by the US and Israel’s war on Iran. The conflict, which began in February, led to a jump in oil prices after the Strait of Hormuz, the main trade route for about 20 per cent of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas, was blockaded by Iran in response. This is still affecting petrol prices and household gas bills, and has seen countries around the world turn to alternative fuel types to boost energy security. Advertisement Read more Solar energy is going to power the world much sooner than you think Around 38.2 gigatonnes of CO2 are expected to be emitted in 2026 globally, according to the latest annual Global Carbon Budget – put together by more than 140 researchers. This is a 0.4 per cent decrease on the previous year, largely due to a projected 1.9 per cent fall in emissions from oil. The drop in oil use was partly offset by a 0.6 per cent increase in emissions from coal. Robbie Andrew at climate research group CICERO in Oslo, Norway, one of the report authors, says financial pressures due to the energy shock are likely to have caused the drop in emissions this year, which may turn out to be a “blip”. “On the assumption that there are no further crises, then you’d expect that emissions would bounce back,” says Andrew. The two biggest dips in emissions in the 21st century have been attributed to the covid-19 pandemic, which saw emissions drop by around 6 per cent in 2020, and the global financial crisis, which saw emissions drop around 2 per cent in 2009. The future outlook depends on how long the energy shock lasts, says Andrew, with governments forced to look at the economic case for continuing to subsidise fossil fuels. The rollout of renewable energy also played a part in bringing down carbon emissions. Electric vehicles and solar and wind power are predicted to offset 64 to 79 per cent of increasing emissions from demand growth through to 2028. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter In China, the world’s biggest emitter of CO2, emissions are projected to decrease by 0.9 per cent in 2026 as the country continues to make strides with expanding renewable energy and electric vehicles. “What’s keeping emissions down is the renewable energy, and the price of oil actually suppresses this even more,” says Corinne Le Quéré at the University of East Anglia, UK, who also worked on the report. “So, that’s encouraging in a way, but it does mean that if the price of oil rebounds to pre-Iran [conflict] levels, most likely the emissions will rebound as well until we have enough further acceleration in renewable energy to really bring the emissions down durably.” Journal Reference: Nature Climate Change DOI: 10.1038/s41558-026-02821-8

item.description: …Says action will worsen hardship, urges dialogue over withheld council funds By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The World Institute for Peace (WIP), a civil society organisation, has criticised the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) in Osun State over its decision to embark on a three-day sympathy strike in support of the Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees (NULGE), describing the action as unnecessary and counterproductive. The strike, which commenced on Monday, followed the NLC’s directive to its affiliate unions to protest the continued withholding of local government allocations amid the prolonged political dispute between the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) over control of local government administration in the state. The industrial action resulted in the closure of schools and public offices across the state as workers complied with the directive. Reacting to the development, WIP Executive Director, Lamina Kamiludeen, said the strike would further compound the economic difficulties facing residents without resolving the lingering local government crisis. Addressing journalists in Osogbo on Monday, Kamiludeen urged the labour unions to pursue dialogue and an out-of-court settlement, noting that the dispute was already before courts of competent jurisdiction. He argued that organised labour should prioritise constructive engagement among the parties rather than shutting down public institutions, particularly schools. According to him, the labour movement should serve as the voice of workers and vulnerable members of society, while demonstrating an understanding of legal and judicial processes in handling disputes. Kamiludeen said the unions could engage the parties involved in the dispute to explore an amicable resolution that would allow the release of the disputed local government funds. He also suggested that the labour leaders could leverage their reported inclusion in President Bola Tinubu’s Presidential Campaign Council, as announced by Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, to facilitate dialogue among the political stakeholders. “The option we would have expected from the labour unions is constructive dialogue with all parties involved in the ongoing litigations. The unions should persuade the parties to either withdraw the cases or consider an out-of-court settlement that would pave the way for the resolution of the impasse surrounding local government funds in Osun State,” he said. Kamiludeen appealed to the unions to reconsider the strike, warning that its consequences would be borne largely by ordinary residents, particularly pupils whose education had been disrupted. item.title: Canada makes rural immigration programme permanent
item.description: By Favour Ulebor Canada has made its Rural Community Immigration Pilot a permanent programme to attract and retain skilled foreign workers in smaller communities facing persistent labour shortages. The Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship, Lena Metlege Diab, announced the decision on Monday, November 9, 2026, in Pictou County, Nova Scotia. According to a statement published on the website of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), the programme will initially retain the 14 communities currently participating in the pilot, with plans to expand to more communities in the future. The employer- and community-driven programme is designed to address labour shortages in rural areas by connecting skilled foreign workers and their families with employers and community support services. It also seeks to encourage newcomers to settle permanently in smaller communities and contribute to their economic development. Speaking during the announcement, Diab said the government recognised the critical role rural communities played in Canada’s economy despite the challenges they faced in attracting workers. “Our government understands that rural communities play a critical role in powering Canada’s economy. At the same time, many face real challenges finding the workers they need. “That’s why we’re transitioning our successful rural immigration pilot into a permanent program—helping smaller communities attract and retain essential workers who deliver services and drive economic growth. “We appreciate that a one-size-fits-all approach to immigration doesn’t work for rural Canada, and this permanent pathway is one part of our work to ensure that communities of all sizes can share in the benefits of responsible, sustainable immigration,” she said. Under Canada’s 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, the government has allocated 5,500 admission spaces to the permanent Rural Community Immigration Program. The government said the initiative was part of its broader immigration policy aimed at stabilising the number of immigrants admitted into the country, reducing the temporary resident population and retaining skilled foreign workers already contributing to local communities. It added that preliminary results from the pilot showed that foreign workers had helped address labour shortages in critical sectors, including healthcare, education, sales and services, between 2025 and 2026. The department also disclosed that participating communities had vetted and designated more than 1,950 trusted employers experiencing persistent labour shortages that could not be addressed through the local workforce between January 2025 and August 2026. The transition to a permanent programme is expected to provide rural employers with a more reliable supply of skilled foreign workers while supporting the long-term economic development of participating communities. The post Canada makes rural immigration programme permanent appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Anthropic's super bug-finding Mythos model is going into Cisco and IBM products
item.description: Anthropic has started extending access to its bug-finding Mythos model by allowing Cisco and IBM to make it part of their security products. Cisco announced its integration today at an event in Melbourne, Australia, where it revealed that the red teaming tools in its AI Defense suite, which looks for weaknesses and inappropriate activity in AI models, agents, and applications they power, will be able to call Mythos to test customers’ setups. “At a very high level, AI Defense has the ability to look at models and break them,” said Jeff Schultz, Cisco’s senior vice president for portfolio strategy and marketing. He said the tool is now “super-charged by Mythos” and will identify more danger that AI Defense will then address. AI Defense already uses AI-powered red teaming to find flaws. Mythos will become another option. Cisco will make it available under users’ existing licenses, without additional cost. Natalie Mead, Anthropic’s head of applied AI for the Asia-Pacific, said the company has a long queue of buyers who want to use Mythos, and working with Cisco will make it easier to satisfy that demand. Anthropic initially made Mythos available under "Project Glasswing," a program that gave vetted organizations access to the model to test their codebases, but has since expanded access through other controlled programs, an arrangement that makes considerable sense because in the wrong hands Mythos could help attackers exploit software flaws. The Cisco deal exposes the functionality of Mythos to end-users, without letting them use the model itself. The Register asked Mead if Anthropic has similar deals with other third parties and she demurred. That may be because a few hours after Cisco told us about its use of Mythos, IBM announced that it will also integrate Anthropic’s model into a product – namely its Concert tool, which uses AI to scan applications for risks and weaknesses. IBM says it will use Mythos “to uncover weaknesses traditional scanners miss, determine which pose real risk and generate fixes for developer approval.” We have asked Anthropic if these integrations represent a decision to open Mythos to more users in more ways. We will update this story if we receive a substantial response. Also on Monday, Anthropic introduced version 5.2 of Mythos and Fable, which the company says generate outputs up to 30 percent faster than version 5.1 yet cost less: $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. Users can choose to run both models in “fast mode,” which speeds up token generation by up to 2.5 times, and doubles prices to $16 per million input tokens and $80 per million output tokens. Anthropic says it “ran extensive prerelease safety testing on the model that underlies Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2. This included developing novel evaluations that give deeper insight into specific concerning behaviors like sandbox escapes.” After those tests, the company concluded “high-stakes risks from misalignment remain low, and the model pe

item.title: The Architecture of Becoming
item.description: A Review of Tomileye E. Abolaji’s The Things Life Taught My Heart By Femi Morgan Published by i2X Media , 2026 Number of pages: 62 pages There is a moment in Tomileye E. Abolaji’s debut collection that captures the entire book of poetry. The book shows that the poet persona is lost in a new city, following the blue dot on her phone, and finds herself travelling fifteen minutes in the wrong direction. “I had not found my way,” she writes. “I had simply travelled farther from it.” It is a simple observation, almost throwaway, yet it contains the essential grammar of this book: the recognition that getting lost is not the same as being defeated, that the wrong road can still teach you something about the right one. It also hints that technology cannot replace intuition. The Things Life Taught My Heart , subtitled Twenty journeys through love, betrayal, courage, discovery and the beautiful art of BECOMING , is a collection of twenty prose poems that trace a life from its difficult beginnings to its hard-won flourishing. Abolaji, a legal counsel and performance poet who has performed in Nigeria and the UK, writes with the precision of someone trained to weigh evidence and the tenderness of someone who has learned that not all truths can be proven in a courtroom. The collection is structured into five movements, “The Wounds We Carry,” “The Things Love Leaves Behind,” “The Value of Being Seen,” “Learning to Stand,” and “Becoming More.” This architecture gives the book a satisfying arc and extends the metaphor of the collection to its structure. We begin in hurt and end in hope, but the journey is never simplistic. Abolaji understands that healing is not linear, that the wounds we carry do not disappear simply because we have learned to name them. The opening piece, “The Courage Hidden in a No,” sets the tone. A friendship dissolves when the speaker refuses a loan the poet persona cannot afford to give. The refusal is met not with understanding but with recrimination: “I became stingy, unfriendly, a terrible person in stories I had never been invited to hear.” What makes this poem remarkable is its refusal to apologise for the boundary drawn. “Kindness should never require the destruction of one’s peace,” Abolaji writes, and the line lands with the force of a verdict. The poem ends with a question that is really a declaration: “if my no makes me a stranger in a friendship that only understands yes, perhaps I have not lost as much as I once feared.” This is a book about learning to trust one’s own judgment, and Abolaji returns to this theme repeatedly. In “The Day Friendship Changed the Locks,” a roommate’s betrayal arrives not through confrontation but through a telephone call to the speaker’s sister, a detail that captures the peculiar cowardice of certain betrayals, the way they hide behind other people. “Some people share your childhood but not your convictions,” Abolaji observes. “Some share your room but not your understanding of friendship.” The li

item.title: We want to produce self-reliant graduates, not job seekers – Skyline varsity
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf Skyline University Nigeria says it is focused on producing self-reliant graduates equipped with practical skills, entrepreneurial knowledge and industry experience to create employment opportunities rather than depend solely on paid jobs. The Vice-Chancellor of the university, Prof. Ajith Kumar V. V., stated this on Monday during a press briefing ahead of the institution’s fifth convocation ceremony scheduled for November 14, 2026. He said the university was committed to equipping students with the knowledge, skills and values required to meet the demands of the modern world. Kumar explained that the institution had continued to strengthen its academic programmes through technology-driven learning, entrepreneurship and partnerships with industries. He said the university established an Entrepreneurship, Innovation and AI Lab to encourage students to develop business ideas, create innovative solutions and establish technology-based enterprises capable of addressing real-life challenges. “We established the Entrepreneurship, Innovation and AI Lab to encourage our students to develop business ideas, create innovative solutions and establish technology-based businesses that can solve real-life problems,” he said. The vice-chancellor also highlighted the university’s collaboration with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) to assist student entrepreneurs in registering their businesses. According to him, the institution has introduced mandatory professional certification courses for all students every semester to strengthen their professional competencies and improve their employability. He added that industry experts would deliver 10 per cent of the university’s curriculum to expose students to practical knowledge and professional experience. Kumar further disclosed that the university had introduced new academic programmes, including B.Sc. Artificial Intelligence, B.Sc. Public Health Science, and B.Sc. Islamic Economics and Finance, following approval by the National Universities Commission (NUC). He said Skyline University was the first university in North-West Nigeria to receive approval to offer a degree programme in Artificial Intelligence. The vice-chancellor also announced that 236 students would graduate at the institution’s fifth convocation, comprising 183 bachelor’s degree graduates, 41 higher-degree graduates and 12 doctorate graduates. He said the ceremony would also mark the first time the university would confer doctorate degrees since its establishment in 2018. “We are making history this year as we confer doctorate degrees for the first time since the university was established in 2018. We have also awarded 50 per cent scholarships to all our top-performing graduates to enable them to pursue postgraduate studies at the university,” he said. item.title: France blames Iran for supermarket hack meltdowns
item.description: France has turned up the heat on Iran over destructive cyberattacks targeting refrigeration controllers at more than 700 grocery stores in October, spoiling food and sparking fires. The country vowed to take action using “all available means of response.” The supermarket attacks , which affected Casino, Leclerc, Coopérative U, Metro, Carrefour, and Intermarché groups, started at least 15 fires and caused food losses in the tens of millions of euros, according to a Monday report by France’s Cyber Crisis Coordination Centre (C4). The C4 includes the National Cybersecurity Agency of France, the Directorate General for External Security, the Directorate General for Internal Security, the Directorate General for Armament, and the Cyber Defence Command. “This is an unprecedented campaign in terms of its scale and level of aggressiveness, thus constituting the first cyber offensive campaign carried out purely for the purpose of sabotage on national territory,” France’s Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs said in a statement . All signs point to CyberAv3ngers Both the report and the statement attributed the refrigeration controller hacks to the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ (IRGC) Shahid Kaveh cyber unit. The Shahid Kaveh unit, which French national security officials say is led by Reza Salarvand and Mahdi Lashgarian, is better known by its hacktivist personas, including CyberAv3ngers . This is the same crew suspected of involvement in the July attacks that targeted more than 100 internet-exposed water systems in America. While the US government hasn’t attributed the intrusions to any country or group, private-sector security analysts blamed Iran , and specifically CyberAv3ngers . The IRGC-affiliated hacking crew has been breaking into industrial controllers for years , and in 2023, American national security and law enforcement agencies attributed a series of cyberattacks against "multiple" US water facilities to CyberAv3ngers. “The Iranian cyber threat against French interests is not new,” according to the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. “Iran has already carried out several destabilizing acts against us, notably targeting the weekly magazine Charlie Hebdo in 2023 and the organization of the Paris Olympic Games in 2024.” Since at least June 2024, the Shahid Kaveh unit has had the ability to scan, access, and control industrial control equipment from Schneider Electric, Siemens, and Rockwell, the French government said in its report. It pins the refrigeration controller hacks on this particular Iranian crew for a couple of reasons. Making the case for attribution First: the infrastructure used to carry out the October supermarket attacks was also used during this timeframe to conduct reconnaissance on Schneider Electric equipment, zeroing in on small- and medium-sized energy and water production units. “The techniques used during these actions are known to have been used by the Shahid Kaveh unit since at least April 2026,” the

item.title: Rubies on Mars?
item.description: Explore This Section Perseverance Home Mission Overview Rover Components Mars Rock Samples Where is Perseverance? Ingenuity Mars Helicopter Mission Updates Science Overview Objectives Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Perseverance Raw Images Images Videos Audio More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home This heavily pitted, light-toned float rock “Nhlanguleni” was imaged by SHERLOC’s WATSON camera on Sol 2023, October 29, 2026, at “Kapama Karula” in the “South Idubi” region. NASA/JPL-Caltech Written by Roger C. Wiens, SuperCam Principal Investigator for NASA’s Perseverance rover at Purdue University Nov. 4, 2026 Exploration on Mars turns up the unexpected. Perseverance is equipped with a fantastic set of instruments for studying the rock record of this ancient planet. Both PIXL and SuperCam have great capabilities for detecting all kinds of elements. SHERLOC, SuperCam, and PIXL can detect minerals using various techniques including x-ray fluorescence, Raman, and infrared spectroscopies. As a side benefit of the way SuperCam performs its Raman spectroscopy, it can also study time-resolved luminescence. Normally luminescence occurs over a broad wavelength range (most of Earth’s commercial lighting uses luminescence in some way or another). Two years ago, the SuperCam team was startled to find strong, narrow luminescence peaks at two wavelengths of 692.7 and 694.1 nanometers when they shot a light-colored rock with the laser. This luminescence comes from delayed atomic transitions in chromium atoms present in a corundum mineral structure. SuperCam can time the delay of the atomic transitions via the resulting photons, and so we could verify that this emission came from chromium in corundum. The results were published in Geophysical Research Letters by a team led by Ann Ollila earlier this year, so you can read all about it. The gemstone version of chromium-containing corundum is ruby. Prior to installing SuperCam on Perseverance, we placed a ruby in the laser beam and watched the entire room pulse a brilliant red as SuperCam’s laser beam hit the gemstone; it was extremely bright. While we haven’t found collectable rubies on Mars yet, the little corundum crystals are helping us learn more about Mars’ past. Corundum is a metamorphic and pegmatitic mineral which we would not expect to find on Mars, a planet that lacks plate tectonics. However, large meteor and asteroid impacts can create local metamorphism due to long-term heating from the impact. Because we are in a very ancient terrain near the rim of Jezero crater, we can expect some evidence of localized metamorphism. As the first mission in such terrain, we are learning new things. Earlier in the mission we tried this technique only rarely; lately we have carried out the time-resolved luminescence observations frequently on light-toned rocks to look for more evid

item.title: Newest Sample, Oldest Rock?
item.description: Explore This Section Perseverance Home Mission Overview Rover Components Mars Rock Samples Where is Perseverance? Ingenuity Mars Helicopter Mission Updates Science Overview Objectives Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Perseverance Raw Images Images Videos Audio More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home NASA’s Mars Perseverance rover acquired this image of the rock sample “Singita” inside the rover’s coring bit using its left Mastcam-Z camera. The image was acquired on Oct. 24, 2026 (Sol 2018), at a local mean solar time of 12:56:57, shortly after the coring operation. NASA/JPL-Caltech/ASU Written by Tasha Coelho, Mastcam-Z Student Collaborator at Arizona State University Nov. 1, 2026 Perseverance’s most recent abrasion “Pumbe” bears a striking resemblance to an earlier abrasion, “ Badger Peak .” That’s no coincidence. As previously reported , that rock had a hardness too high to core. However, the team felt strongly that it was worth the effort to add a gabbro, an igneous rock made mostly of calcium-rich plagioclase feldspar and pyroxene crystals, to Perseverance’s sample collection . In search of a new local gabbroic candidate to sample, Perseverance traveled about 100 meters (330 feet) to a different patch of light-toned rocks . Indeed, visual and chemical data from the light-toned rocks in the new workspace revealed a composition similar to that of “Badger Peak.” NASA’s Mars Perseverance rover acquired this image of the abrasion patch “Pumbe” using its SHERLOC WATSON camera, located on the turret at the end of the rover’s robotic arm. The image was acquired on Oct. 17, 2026 (Sol 2011), at a local mean solar time of 16:14:35. The abrasion patch is about 5 centimeters (2 inches) across. NASA/JPL-Caltech To improve the odds of collecting a sample this time, the team made prudent decisions: choosing a neighboring rock with a flatter surface better oriented for the drill stabilizers to press against, and using a coring bit with less wear. At last, in a display of the rover’s namesake quality, the drill made it about 3.1 centimeters (1.2 inches) into the rock. Sample acquisition activities followed, making “Singita” the rover’s first sample in more than a year. While Singita is the newest sample, it may be among the oldest rocks in Perseverance’s collection . Textures in the rock suggest that it likely formed deep in the crust and was modified and excavated by at least one, and possibly multiple, large impact events. Perseverance has now completed its 66 th successful abrasion and collected an intriguing new sample alongside it. The latest mission status report opens with “Perseverance remains healthy and stable on Mars” and lists “Spacecraft Status: Nominal.” Translation: the rover remains capable of continued fruitful exploration, with many more abrasions to come. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 9, 1967: NASA launches the Saturn V moon rocket for the first time on Apollo 4, but no astronauts were aboard
item.description: null On Nov. 9, 1967, NASA launched the powerful new Saturn V rocket on its maiden voyage. The Saturn V moon rocket was 363 feet tall. That's taller than the Statue of Liberty! It was the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built at the time (though SpaceX's Starship megarocket has since surpassed it). NASA needed such a powerful rocket to launch astronauts to the moon. However, the first Saturn V launch didn't carry astronauts, because it was only a test flight. During the launch, the rocket created a loud shockwave that surprised nearby observers. The ground shook so hard that it rattled buildings miles away, and all the shaking caused a huge shower of dust and debris NASA's new launch center, the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The mission lasted 8 hours 36 minutes. The rocket carried an uncrewed command module that splashed down in the Pacific Ocean. NASA's first-ever Saturn V rocket launches on its maiden flight from Cape Canaveral, Florida on the uncrewed Apollo 4 test flight on Nov. 9, 1967. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered The launch of Apollo 4 in November 1967 was a turning point for NASA on its path to landing astronauts on the moon. The space agency had bet the moon on its new Saturn V booster, a three-stage heavy-lift rocket designed to fly astronauts in a capsule (as well as their lander) to the moon and back. But the rocket had never been fully tested until the Apollo 4 launch. NASA also needed a new launch site for its Apollo missions. So the agency built Launch Complex 39 at what is now called the Kennedy Space Center, a Florida spaceport that has become the home port for orbital human spaceflight in the United States. But in 1967, no rockets had ever flown from the site. Yet, everything went according to plan. Amazing Apollo 4: NASA's 1st Saturn V Moon Rocket Test Flight in Photos “It was really an expert launching all the way through from lifting off exactly on time to performance of every single stage,” rocket pioneer Wernher von Braun , director of NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, said at the time . The launch came as NASA was on its heels. Just months earlier, on Jan. 27, 1967, the space agency suffered a fatal tragedy when Apollo 1 astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee died on the launch pad after a fire broke out inside their Apollo command module during a ground test. A view of the Apollo 4 launch after stage separation looking back down at Earth from the Saturn V rocket. NASA/Interm Archives/Getty The uncrewed Apollo 4 command module splashes down under parachutes after a smooth test flight. NASA/Interm Archives/Getty “The maiden voyage of the Saturn V dramatically increased the confidence of people across the nation in the management of the largest research and development undertaking in which the western world has ever engaged,” George Mueller, NASA's then-Associate Administrator for Manned Space Flight, said at the time . item.title: Jupiter and Mars are set for a breathtaking close approach later this week: Here's how to see it
item.description: null Jupiter and Mars will shine side by side in a spectacular close approach in the heart of the constellation Leo on Nov. 15. Here's what you need to know. Mars and Jupiter reach their closest apparent separation in Earth's sky at 9:04 p.m. EST on Nov. 15 (0204 GMT on Nov. 16), according to astronomy website In-The-Sky . The planets will be below the horizon for U.S. stargazers at the moment of their closest approach, but observers can catch the pair rising above the eastern horizon around midnight local time, just a few hours later. Remember: You can discover the exact timings for the rising and setting of the planets above your local horizon using Time and Date's night sky tracker . Jupiter will be the brightest of the pair, when it rises a little over 1 degree from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your little finger held at arm's length against the night sky. The bright star Regulus will glow close at hand, forming the dot of the backward question mark formation of stars that represents the head of the great Lion in the constellation Leo. Celestron StarSense Explorer LT114AZ (Image credit: Celestron) The Celestron StarSense Explorer LT114AZ is a great way to get a closer look at Jupiter, Mars and Saturn. Its 4.5-inch aperture and a high 1000mm focal length delivers good magnification out of the box, plus it's integrated with the StarSense smartphone app, which makes finding those planets so much easier. Check out our full review for more. Mars and Jupiter will be close enough to share the field of view of a pair of 10x50 binoculars and will also make for a spectacular sight through the eyepiece of a telescope when viewed separately as they rise away from the horizon. The gas giant's iconic Great Red Spot will rotate into view in the predawn hours of Nov. 16, and will be visible through a backyard telescope with an aperture of just 4 inches . Using a light green color filter will help increase the visibility of the vast storm, while an orange filter will help bring out detail in the gas giant's sweeping cloud belts. The two planets will appear to gradually drift apart over the coming weeks and won't appear as close again for another 2.5 years in July 2029 , when the two planets appear close together in the constellation Virgo . Be sure to check out our guide to photographing the night sky , along with our picks of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography if you're interested in following the dance of the planets for yourself. Editor's Note: If you would like to share your astrophotography with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

item.title: DCU shake-up: James Gunn and Peter Safran out post-merger
item.description: It's barely been two months since the controversial Paramount and Warner Bros. merger, and we've already got a shockingly unexpected ouster : Co-CEOs of the rebooted DC Universe, James Gunn and Peter Safran, are stepping down from that role despite the Hollywood rumor mill assuming that the duo would be safe. It's unclear whether the pair chose to resign or were forced out, or what will happen to their planned slate of projects beyond 2028's Superman: Man of Tomorrow , which is in post-production. Producer Jeremy Latcham—a protege of Marvel's Kevin Feige who worked with Gunn on Guardians of the Galaxy among other MCU films—will replace them. Per Gunn and Safran's joint statement : Four years ago, we set out to unite DC under one creative vision. In that time, we helped restore Superman to the heart of DC, while opening new doors and telling new stories in film and television with Peacemaker , Creature Commandos, Lanterns and Clayface. We’re immensely proud of the team that turned that ambition into something real, including the actors, crews and executives we had the opportunity to collaborate with. We’ve shared a creative history with Jeremy going back to Marvel, and we’re eager to see the perspective he brings to DC’s next chapter. We’re excited to return to what drew us to this job in the first place, which is telling the stories we love, including the next chapter of Clark and Lex’s journey in Man of Tomorrow . DCU fans are mourning the news and what it could mean for the franchise. My feelings are mixed. On the one hand, I'm on record that I’ve found the rebooted DC Universe films released thus far to be enjoyable but rather forgettable, even when the positives outweigh the negatives . (I have yet to see Clayface , which debuted to good reviews and a solid box office showing.) But HBO has done right by the DCU: I loved both seasons of Peacemaker; Lanterns is a shining beacon of what is possible when someone is allowed to get really creative within the genre; and I'm very much looking forward to next year's Jimmy Olsen (Skylar Gisondo) series The People v. Gorilla Grodd —described as a “mockumentary crime comedy superhero series.” Read full article Comments

item.title: Tinubu, Atiku, Obi Will Collapse Under Their Own Weight — SDP’s Adewole
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Adewole Adebayo, has said he is confident of victory in a free, fair, and credible 2027 election. Adebayo said that other candidates like President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Atiku Abubakar of the Africa Democratic Party (ADC) and Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Party (NDC) will fall under their own weight. Speaking during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, he said that his manifesto, Farewell to Poverty and Insecurity, is a pathway to progress and good governance that can be deployed to improve the lives of Nigerians “They will collapse under their own weight; that is not the issue. What I want to defeat is poverty and insecurity. “But to defeat that, you need to defeat ignorance in people going to just vote based on sentiment or looking for something,” Adebayo said. “You also have to defeat lethargy where people get tired, ‘Oh, my vote doesn’t count. You also have to defeat apathy. “So, once we do that, we will defeat anybody. When we say defeat, it’s not a wrestling match; it’s about convincing the majority of your fellow citizens to believe in this plan. To say this plan is going to work.” Adebayo says his manifesto will improve the lives of Nigerians. According to him, fixing the government will fix the security challenges in the country. The SDP candidate said that Nigerians should not see terrorists anymore in six months, given the capacity of the Nigerian Armed Forces. Adewole promises to address banditry, saying that citizens will get security as a Christmas present in 2027. The presidential election is scheduled to be held on January 16, 2027. The post Tinubu, Atiku, Obi Will Collapse Under Their Own Weight — SDP’s Adewole appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Chioma Ude Celebrates Women in African Cinema at AFRIFF 15 Dinner | See Photos
item.description: For AFRIFF’s 15th anniversary, Chioma Ude made room for a different kind of celebration: an intimate dinner dedicated to the women shaping African cinema. The gathering brought together female filmmakers, producers and directors for an evening of fashion, good food and conversations about the industry they are helping to shape, with plenty of opportunities to catch up and connect outside the usual festival setting. As founder and executive director of the Africa International Film Festival, Chioma established AFRIFF in 2010 to showcase African talent and create more opportunities for filmmakers to reach wider audiences. Fifteen years on, the festival has become an important platform for African cinema, making the dinner a fitting occasion to celebrate some of the women contributing to the industry. The evening also came with a specially curated dining experience by Chef Tolu Eros whose multi-course menu brought West African flavours into a fine-dining setting. Alongside the conversations and fashion, the dinner offered guests a chance to enjoy good food and celebrate the women whose work continues to shape African storytelling. item.description: The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nentawe Yilwatda, has dismissed concerns about President Bola Tinubu’s health ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that the President is fit to contest. The APC chairman stated this on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday. ﻿ He urged Nigerians not to interpret isolated expressions of dissent against the President as evidence of widespread unpopularity. Addressing concerns about Tinubu’s limited attendance at some presidential campaign rallies, Yilwatda said the President could not be expected to participate in every campaign activity while discharging his constitutional responsibilities. He said some public officials had been advised to attend selected rallies rather than all the engagements to prevent governance from suffering. Following Tinubu’s earlier announcement that he would not attend every campaign rally because of the responsibilities of his office, the APC chairman said the President’s absence should not be interpreted as a sign of weakness or inability to lead the party’s re-election effort. Muslim-Muslim Ticket Yilwatda also defended the Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket of Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima, dismissing concerns that the arrangement would marginalise Christians under the APC administration. He maintained that Christians had continued to have their voices heard in government, adding that those the party had engaged were comfortable with the arrangement. “Most Christians that we’ve engaged and we’ve spoken to them, they are very okay with the Muslim-Muslim ticket,” he said. “The thought and the fear of most Christians was that the Muslim-Muslim ticket may suppress their voices, but their voices are heard loud and clear now.” He also argued that Christians had not suffered molestation because of Tinubu’s religion during the President’s three years in office. ADC Crisis Reacting to the Federal High Court judgment invalidating the David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), the APC chairman denied that his party had any involvement in the opposition party’s internal crisis. He questioned why the ADC was blaming the ruling party over a legal dispute instituted by one of its members. Asked whether he was pleased that the ADC was facing a leadership crisis, Yilwatda said he was not bothered by the development. Yilwatda expressed confidence that Tinubu would defeat Atiku in a free and fair election. He argued that Atiku’s performance in the 2023 presidential election was largely attributable to the political structure of the PDP rather than his individual popularity. “He did not win because of Atiku; he won because of the structure of the PDP. It was the PDP that brought Atiku, not Atiku winning on his own,” he said.
